suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Credential Exfiltration via Environment Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing worm hidden in…compromised npm packages.' Post-install scripts execute with inherited process environment containing AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, and other sensitive values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node/npm child processes spawned during package installation that read environment variables programmatically or export secrets, followed by outbound HTTPS POST to domains not in org whitelist within 60 seconds. Correlate package version against registry publish timestamps.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Registry Republishing—Maintainer Compromise or Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'automatically spread…by republishing malicious updates' to 400+ packages. Indicates compromised maintainer credentials or token theft enabling unauthorized version releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm registry API auth (registry.npmjs.org/v2/auth or npm token validation) from unusual geolocation or ISP, followed by publish operation (POST /package) on dormant maintainer accounts. Flag version timestamps misaligned with git commit history.

suggestion.title: Package Version Anomaly—Rapid Iteration or Downgrade Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Malicious republishing suggests unusual version sequencing: jumps in patch semver, timestamps out of order, or versions released outside maintenance windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package-lock.json locked versions against published registry history; flag downloads of versions with no git tag, commits, or GitHub release. Detect patch-level jumps (1.0.5 → 1.0.250) or versions released at atypical frequencies (sub-hour intervals).

suggestion.title: Self-Propagating Worm—Horizontal Spread via Sibling Package Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'self-propagating worm.' Malware within one package modifies peer or downstream node_modules to inject itself, enabling geometric spread across dependency chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node processes writing to node_modules/*/package.json or */index.js outside their own directory scope. Detect child npm/node processes executing publish commands from within node_modules. Correlate file write timestamps with subsequent registry API calls.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration to C2 Infrastructure Post-npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing worm' implies harvested secrets (npm tokens, API keys, cloud credentials) sent to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TLS/HTTPS connections from node.exe to non-RFC1918 IPs initiated within 120 seconds of npm install, especially to recently-registered domains. Inspect TLS SNI/certificate issuer; flag connections to IPs with no reverse DNS or to known C2 hosting providers.

suggestion.title: npm Dependency Lock-File Modification Without Git Commit
suggestion.rationale: Worm may alter package-lock.json or yarn.lock to inject malicious version constraints, ensuring subsequent installs pull compromised packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when package-lock.json or yarn.lock is modified by non-standard git operations (direct file writes, npm cache operations) or when modification timestamp predates nearest git commit by >5 minutes. Cross-reference with npm registry to confirm versions in lock file exist in registry with matching publish timestamps.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OAuth Refresh Endpoint Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states POST /api/v1/oauth2-credential/refresh/:credentialId 'requires no authentication' and returns access_token directly. Pipeline omitted direct detection for this exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to paths matching **/oauth2-credential/refresh/** or **/oauth**/refresh* that lack authentication headers (no Bearer token, session cookie, or API key) and result in HTTP 200 with token-bearing JSON response. Flag any single source IP making >2 refresh requests in 5 minutes across distinct credentialIds.

suggestion.title: OAuth Provider Refresh Token Abuse from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker obtaining refresh_token and using it to call the OAuth provider. Detect abnormal refresh token usage patterns: 'sends a refresh request to the configured OAuth provider' from sources not matching legitimate application infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate refresh token requests to OAuth providers (Google, Microsoft, GitHub, etc.) against known Flowise application IPs/infrastructure. Alert on refresh token requests originating from ASNs, geolocations, or ISPs outside the organization's footprint or deployment regions. Baseline refresh frequency per credentialId and alert on >5x deviations in 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: Credential Decryption Without User Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint 'decrypts the stored credential'. Detect application-layer credential decryption events not triggered by user action or maintenance workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Flowise application logs for decrypt/key-retrieval operations on oauth2_credential table. Alert if decryption events occur outside scheduled maintenance windows, without corresponding user login or API auth header, or at unusual frequency (>10 decrypts/hour per credentialId). Correlate with source IP to detect non-admin access.

suggestion.title: Post-Token-Theft Lateral Movement via Stolen OAuth Session
suggestion.rationale: Article impact: 'enables token theft for any connected service'. Detect downstream use of stolen OAuth tokens: legitimate cloud services (Slack, GitHub, Google Workspace) accessed immediately after token refresh, from atypical source IPs or user agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For services integrated via OAuth to Flowise (Slack, GitHub, Google, etc.), correlate refresh token generation to subsequent API calls using that access_token from anomalous IP addresses. Build a baseline of typical source IPs per OAuth credential; flag calls from new IPs within 5 minutes of token refresh. Monitor for privilege escalation post-auth (e.g., creating repos, adding collaborators, accessing org-level secrets).

suggestion.title: Flowise OAuth Credential Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires guessing or discovering :credentialId values to exploit. Detect brute-force or enumeration attempts against the refresh endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to /api/v1/oauth2-credential/refresh/* with varying :credentialId values from single source IP. Alert on >10 distinct credentialId attempts in 5-minute window, especially with HTTP 404/403/200 response variation suggesting ID discovery. Cross-check against known credentialId patterns if predictable.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-70478 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' as a recommended hunt using template. Pipeline failed to generate this standard IOC-driven hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Flowise installations with version <vulnerable_version>. Cross-reference with internet-facing asset data (Shodan, Censys, internal port scans). Flag Flowise instances exposed on public IPs or accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate with successful HTTP 200 responses to **/oauth2-credential/refresh/** endpoints from external source IPs.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage ransomware attack chain interrupted pre-encryption
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'multi-stage attack' and 'before the payload could persist or spread,' establishing a detection opportunity during execution/persistence phase before impact. No use case was generated for this core attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multi-process execution chains where a child process spawns unusual services, registry modifications, or file-write operations consistent with ransomware staging. Alert on process lineage anomalies (e.g., explorer.exe → cmd.exe → powershell.exe → service creation) within a 30-second window; combine with file entropy spikes or binary staging in %temp%.

suggestion.title: Rapid endpoint isolation triggered by behavioral anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states Defender 'automatically isolated a compromised endpoint in 129 seconds'—a clear detection→response timeline. No use case was generated for automated isolation rules or behavioral triggers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when endpoint exhibits rapid sequence of indicators within 120 seconds: multiple process spawning from a single parent, suspicious service creation attempts, and network communication to infrastructure not on whitelist. Trigger automatic isolation if behavioral score exceeds threshold.

suggestion.title: Ransomware execution prevented before file encryption
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'before the payload could persist or spread,' indicating the attack was stopped before encryption impact. No use case captured pre-encryption file-operation patterns or executable staging detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume file writes to non-system directories by processes not typically associated with file operations (e.g., rundll32, regsvcs). Alert on file operations preceded by batch file execution or command-line invocation of encryption-utility-like tools (7z, WinRAR, openssl) from user-writable paths.

suggestion.title: AnySign4PC Process Spawning Unsigned Child Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Install Backdoors Without Prompts'—execution phase requires detection of child-process spawning from a trusted signing tool. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AnySign4PC or related signing utilities (asign.exe, anysign4pc.exe) spawning child processes, particularly unsigned executables or LOLBins. Correlate with absence of user interaction events (mouse clicks, keyboard input) preceding execution. Monitor for process creation outside normal business hours or from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Attack: Malware Downloaded from Compromised .KR Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hacked Korean Sites' is the initial access vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs for compromised domains or delivery infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/S downloads originating from .kr domains hosting suspicious payloads. Monitor for redirects from legitimate Korean business/media sites to attacker infrastructure. Alert on downloads of AnySign4PC binaries, certificate files, or related DLLs from non-official mirrors.

suggestion.title: Silent Installation via Suppressed UAC Prompts
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase: 'Without Prompts' indicates defense evasion. Pipeline generated zero defense-evasion detections for prompt suppression techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installer or code-signing processes executed with parameters that suppress user interaction (/quiet, /silent, MSIEXEC /qn, Rundll32 with malicious DLL). Monitor for parent-child process chains bypassing UAC elevation prompts. Cross-reference with absence of UAC event logs (Event ID 4689) when elevation would normally be expected.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Persistence via Run-Key Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Install Backdoors'—implicitly requires persistence. Pipeline generated zero persistence-phase detections for registry abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKCU equivalents initiated by AnySign4PC or child processes. Alert on new run-key values referencing unsigned binaries or legitimate executables in non-standard paths (ProgramData, temp, user AppData). Correlate with suspicious child-process execution.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Code-Signing Tool by Non-Developer Accounts
suggestion.rationale: AnySign4PC is weaponized as an execution mechanism. Pipeline missed the abuse-of-legitimate-tool vector ('Exploit AnySign4PC'). No detections for out-of-policy signing activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when AnySign4PC is executed by non-developer or non-IT service accounts. Detect code-signing activity outside normal business hours or batch-pattern execution. Monitor for rapid, sequential signing of multiple binaries (batch malware signing). Flag signing of binaries in temp directories or PE files with suspicious sections or entropy.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Beaconing to Command & Control Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Install Backdoors'—requires post-exploitation C2 phase. Pipeline generated zero command-and-control phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from AnySign4PC child processes to non-whitelisted IP ranges or to Korean domains not in business scope. Detect periodic, low-volume DNS queries or beaconing patterns (fixed intervals, fixed packet sizes). Alert on connections to newly-registered or high-reputation-anomaly domains from service or system-context processes.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: N-able N-central Public-Facing Instances (CVE-2026-18556)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE-2026-18556 template substitution; pipeline generated zero use cases. Article phrase: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' against exposed N-central deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory N-able N-central instances on public-facing networks or accessible via VPN. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-18556 coverage. Correlate with authentication logs for failed/succeeded login bursts from previously unseen IPs post-discovery, indicating exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass API Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass via alternate path/channel implies attackers probe N-central's auth endpoints or side-channel APIs. Article: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel.' This attack step warranted dedicated detection but pipeline missed it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central HTTP(S) endpoints for unusual HTTP methods (PUT/DELETE on auth paths), path traversal patterns, API calls bypassing expected auth flows (e.g., direct service access without UI), or authentication success immediately following 401/403 responses. Alert on anomalous login success rates from single IPs without prior successful auth history.

suggestion.title: N-central Privilege Escalation & Lateral Movement Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: N-central is remote management/deployment platform; once authentication bypassed, attacker gains legitimate session and can pivot. Article doesn't detail post-compromise steps, but pipeline missed downstream MITRE techniques T1078 (Valid Accounts) and T1133 (External Remote Services).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation: monitor N-central admin consoles for unusual commands (credential export, policy changes, agent redeployment), sessions from IPs without prior admin activity history, or bulk deployments of agents/updates to downstream managed endpoints. Correlate N-central access logs with endpoint activity on managed systems to detect lateral movement or persistence.

suggestion.title: N-central CVE-2026-18556 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-18556 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and notes CISA KEV entries are actively exploited in the wild. Pipeline must surface CVE identifier for scanner rule instantiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-18556 matches on N-able N-central instances. Correlate against patch inventory; any vulnerable instance post-2026-08-07 federal due date indicates non-compliance and active exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: N-central Unauthenticated Access via Alternate Path Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' — core attack vector. Pipeline must construct detection for non-standard authentication routes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central for HTTP/HTTPS requests to /api, /admin, or undocumented paths that complete successfully without prior credential submission events. Flag requests bypassing standard login flow (e.g., session tokens without auth handshake, direct API calls using alternate headers or verb abuse).

suggestion.title: Exposed N-central Internet-Facing Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability is in 'public-facing application' — requires asset enumeration. Pipeline must instantiate asset-exposure hunt cited in article template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: External scan or certificate transparency query for N-central instances exposed to internet. Cross-reference SSL cert subjects, management port defaults (typically 8080/8443), or service banners advertising N-able N-central. Prioritize any exposed instance with software version < announced patch release.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise N-central Lateral Movement via Managed Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies N-central as centralized management platform — successful auth bypass grants control-plane access to managed assets. Requires detection of downstream exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After N-central compromise, watch for unusual outbound commands from N-central to managed endpoints (mass agent deployment, policy modification, command execution). Flag unexpected PowerShell/Cmd execution originated from N-central communication sessions.

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' — this is a direct detection hypothesis. Should hunt for HTTP 401/403 followed by successful access on non-canonical auth endpoints, path traversal payloads, or API auth-bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect N-central web-server requests that bypass standard authentication: patterns include /api/*, /admin, /management, or other alternate endpoint access preceded by failed auth or absent Authorization headers. Look for 401→200 sequences or direct 200 responses on restricted paths.

suggestion.title: N-central Exploitation Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-18556 as exploited in the wild with federal patch due 2026-08-07, implying active scanning/exploitation. Pipeline should detect known exploitation signatures if any POC/malware has been published.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to N-central endpoints with payloads, user-agents, or request patterns known to trigger CVE-2026-18556. Baseline on any public POC or vendor advisory; prioritize external-facing N-central instances.

suggestion.title: N-central Exposed Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references asset-exposure hunts and notes N-central is public-facing application. Pipeline should generate continuous inventory of exposed N-central web interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify N-central instances with public DNS resolution or internet-routable IP addresses. Cross-reference with patch management to flag unpatched instances (versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-18556). This is the asset-exposure baseline mentioned in the article.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise N-central Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes auth bypass to N-central, which is a remote management platform. Once compromised, attacker can abuse N-central's own capabilities to move laterally or persist. Pipeline missed this chaining phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting unauthorized N-central access, hunt for anomalous deployment, agent push, or remote-execution tasks initiated from that session. Look for unusual scale (many targets) or timing (off-hours) for tasks initiated post-breach.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner: CVE-2026-18556 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-18556 — match against your vulnerability scanner' yet pipeline generated zero scanner-based hunts despite this being the primary detection vector for a CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner databases and asset management systems for N-able N-central instances tagged with CVE-2026-18556. Prioritize publicly-routable assets and enforce remediation against federal patch deadline 2026-08-07.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Internet Exposure Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' and implies internet-facing instances are being actively exploited (CISA KEV definition), but pipeline generated no network or exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound connections to N-able N-central standard ports (443, 8443) from external/untrusted IPs. Cross-reference with Shodan/Censys historical records. Flag any connection spikes or new exposures post-2026-08-04 (KEV publication).

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' but pipeline missed detection signatures for actual bypass attempts before system compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central web logs for repeated failed authentication followed by successful session establishment without valid credentials, requests to alternate/undocumented authentication endpoints, or HTTP 401→200 transitions. Baseline normal auth patterns first.

suggestion.title: Post-Bypass Lateral Movement from N-central
suggestion.rationale: Once authentication bypass succeeds, article's implied kill chain progresses to lateral movement, but pipeline captured no post-exploitation detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious RWinRM, RDP, or SSH sessions initiated by N-able N-central service accounts or from the appliance' IP. Detect lateral movement anomalies: unexpected authentication from the appliance, service account logins at atypical hours/locations, or privilege escalation attempts following N-central access.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Service Account Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass vulnerability enables attackers to assume service account privileges; article's 'alternate path' language indicates non-standard authentication paths that evade logging, yet pipeline missed credential-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect re-use of N-able N-central service account credentials outside normal maintenance windows. Hunt for golden ticket or Kerberos token anomalies if the bypass involves directory service interaction. Cross-reference with MFA logs for bypassed MFA.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Endpoint Compromise Signal Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation; article provides no IOCs or malware indicators, but post-bypass behavior (process execution, file creation) should be hunted to detect compromised appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On suspected compromised N-able N-central instances, detect unusual child process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash), file writes to unexpected directories (temp, startup folders), or scheduled task creation by N-central service account.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18556 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Vulnerability: CVE-2026-18556' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with this CVE as the scan signature. Pipeline generated no UC despite this direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all N-able N-central instances (vendor='N-able', product='N-central') that match vulnerability signature CVE-2026-18556 and are externally exposed. Prioritize by exposure vector and patch status. Alert on any scanner hit even if last patch date suggests remediation, as patch lag is emphasized as critical.

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' — this is the core attack vector. Pipeline missed detection of suspicious auth attempts to non-standard N-central endpoints or unusual login patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central login endpoints for authentication attempts using unusual URL paths, query parameters, or HTTP headers that deviate from standard login flows. Flag successful logins immediately following failed attempts to the main auth path, and alert on any POST to non-standard authentication endpoints like '/admin/bypass', '/api/auth/alternate', or paths containing 'channel' or 'alternate'.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized N-central API Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: If auth bypass succeeds, attacker gains access to N-central's management APIs. Article emphasizes N-central is a sensitive remote-access platform; API abuse post-compromise is a critical downstream indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track API calls to N-central endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/systems, /api/agents, /api/commands) from recently-created or dormant accounts, unusual source IPs, or sessions that don't match typical user patterns. Flag bulk agent enumeration or command execution via API shortly after authentication.

suggestion.title: N-central Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes CVE-2026-18556 is 'observed exploited in the wild.' Pipeline should detect active exploitation attempts: malformed auth requests, exploitation payloads, or known proof-of-concept patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to N-central with exploitation signatures: overly-long headers, SQL injection payloads in auth params, path traversal attempts (../ or %2e%2e), or user-agent strings known to be associated with automated scanners. Flag rapid-fire auth attempts from single source within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: N-central Remote Code Execution via Compromise
suggestion.rationale: N-central is a remote management platform; successful auth bypass likely grants attacker ability to push agents or commands to managed systems. This is the business-impact kill-chain link the article implies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track commands or scripts pushed to endpoints via N-central that originate from recently-compromised N-central credentials, unusual admin accounts, or from IP ranges not associated with legitimate N-central management. Flag agent updates, PowerShell invocations, or script deployments initiated immediately after auth-bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: N-central Public Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes N-central is a public-facing application. Pipeline should enumerate all externally-exposed N-central instances to scope attack surface, per CISA KEV mandate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for public-facing N-central instances on internet-routable IPs (ports 8040, 8041, typical N-central ports). Correlate with internal asset inventory to identify misconfigurations. Flag any externally-exposed N-central management console as immediate remediation priority.

suggestion.title: N-central Asset Discovery and Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'N-able N-central' as the vulnerable product, requiring operators to first locate instances. Pipeline missed the foundational hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan logs, asset inventories, and vulnerability scanner reports for N-central instances. Look for published or internal-facing N-central UI fingerprints (login pages, API endpoints). Cross-reference with patch-management systems to confirm exposure.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempts on N-central (CVE-2026-18556)
suggestion.rationale: Core attack path stated as 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'—pipeline should model post-auth detection instead of generic asset hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central authentication logs for: (1) successful logins without corresponding MFA challenges or credential entries, (2) login attempts using alternate paths (e.g., API endpoints, management interfaces bypassing main login), (3) session hijacking or privilege escalation within N-central post-auth.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18556 Vulnerability Scanner Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner'—direct vulnerability scanner correlation is the immediate detection tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable, etc.) with N-central product detection. Flag any instance tagged with N-central that does not have a remediation date prior to federal due date (2026-08-07). Verify scanner output against official advisories to eliminate false negatives from outdated signatures.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Lateral Movement from N-central Compromise
suggestion.rationale: N-able N-central is an MSP management platform; successful authentication bypass gives attacker access to managed client infrastructure. Pipeline missed persistence and lateral-movement implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After identifying N-central compromise, pivot to outbound connections from N-central server (RDP, SSH, WinRM, API calls) to managed client environments. Look for unusual authentication or management commands targeting downstream assets. Cross-correlate with client-side security logs for signs of lateral movement initiated from compromised N-central instance.

suggestion.title: N-central Asset Exposure Hunt (CVE-2026-18556)
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'currently being exploited' via CISA KEV catalog designation. Authentication bypass requires exposed N-central instances as attack surface. Template guidance explicitly directs 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate N-central instances on internet-facing networks and DMZ. Fingerprint via HTTP banner, certificate inspection (N-able branding), or DNS resolution patterns. Cross-reference against N-central version inventory to identify instances running vulnerable builds prior to patch due date 2026-08-07.

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core vulnerability: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'. Exploitation occurs through non-standard authentication routes, not reflected in normal login audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful authentication to N-central API endpoints or URI paths not in standard login flow. Alert on auth success immediately following failed attempts on standard paths. Monitor for requests containing auth-bypass-indicative parameters (e.g., alternate credentials, bearer tokens, API key injection) to non-standard N-central routes.

suggestion.title: N-central Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'alternate path or channel' vulnerability class implies attackers must discover bypass routes. Reconnaissance precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns of HTTP 400/401/403 responses from N-central when probing non-standard URIs, API endpoints, or parameter-tampering attempts. Pattern signature: >5 auth failures to distinct N-central paths within 5-minute window, followed by single 200 OK from same source IP on unexpected endpoint.

suggestion.title: N-central Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: N-central management platform provides visibility and control over customer endpoints in MSP environments. Successful auth bypass enables lateral movement and persistent access deployment across managed estates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post N-central authentication, monitor for anomalous API calls to deploy agents, provision credentials, or modify endpoint configurations. Alert on unexpected N-central API activity targeting customer/managed device populations, especially credential provisioning or agent deployment outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: N-central Patch Compliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites Federal patch due date 2026-08-07 and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Recommends fleet-wide version check regardless of scanner negatives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all N-able N-central instances; correlate with N-central build version against known-vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-18556. Flag instances with patch available but not deployed. Track remediation status against Federal due date for compliance and risk prioritization.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Vulnerable Driver Loading via BYOVD
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions '3-Driver BYOVD Chain'—the core attack vector. Pipeline should detect when vulnerable signed drivers are loaded to bypass kernel security. No UC generated despite this being the primary exploitation method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or suspicious driver loads, especially those matching known vulnerable driver hashes. Correlate driver load with abnormal process context (services.exe, svchost, rundll32 loading drivers from non-standard paths). Flag chains where multiple drivers load sequentially from temp or user-writable locations.

suggestion.title: ValleyRAT Process Execution and C2 Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'ValleyRAT' as the final payload. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs for this malware—no process names, hashes, C2 domains, or command-line patterns. Malware names explicitly in title should trigger IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ValleyRAT execution by process behavior: unusual parent-child chains from loaded vulnerable drivers, spawned cmd.exe/powershell with C2-like network connections (DNS queries to suspicious domains, outbound to uncommon ports). Correlate driver load timing with unexpected process creation.

suggestion.title: Multi-Driver Privilege Escalation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies '3-Driver' chain, implying layered exploitation. No kill-chain phase covering privilege escalation or defense-evasion staging. Pipeline should reconstruct multi-step driver chain: vulnerable driver 1 → load driver 2 → privilege escalation → load driver 3 (payload delivery).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential or clustered driver loads within short time window (< 5 min) from same source process or user context. Monitor for registry modifications related to driver signing, code integrity checks, or boot configuration. Alert on drivers loading with mismatched architecture (x86 on x64 system) or unsigned drivers in protected directories.

suggestion.title: Japanese Manufacturer Network Reconnaissance Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Japanese Manufacturer'—a specific vertical with likely OT/manufacturing systems. Post-BYOVD privilege escalation should trigger discovery and lateral movement. No UCs for reconnaissance or OT-adjacent indicators (SMB scanning, network enumeration from kernel context).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After vulnerable driver loads, watch for unusual SYSTEM/elevated process spawning network tools: nbtstat, net view, arp, ipconfig, route query. Monitor for internal network scans (ICMP, SMB port 445, WinRM 5985) originating from kernel-mode callbacks or LoadImage from known-vulnerable drivers.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: EDR/Security Tool Tampering via Kernel Driver

suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2026-18556'. Pipeline must emit scanner queries for this KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner databases (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) for systems reporting vulnerable N-able N-central versions. Filter by product name 'N-central' and CVE-2026-18556. CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation, so patch status must be reconciled against asset inventory.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'. Pipeline must detect malformed or non-standard authentication attempts against N-central endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central web or API authentication logs for: (a) requests to non-standard or undocumented authentication endpoints, (b) failed auth attempts followed immediately by successful access to administrative endpoints, (c) HTTP 401/403 followed by 200 on alternate paths. Baseline normal auth channels first.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Alternate Authentication Channel Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack uses 'alternate path or channel'—suggests non-primary auth mechanism. Detection must discriminate between normal multi-factor flows and bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag access to N-central administrative or sensitive endpoints via uncommon request patterns: direct API calls without session cookies, requests bypassing load balancer, traffic on non-standard ports or protocols, or requests from internal IP ranges inconsistent with normal client distribution.

suggestion.title: Exposed N-able N-central Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: KEV implies internet-facing deployment. Article references asset-exposure hunt. Pipeline must generate discovery use case for exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query passive DNS and internet scanning services (Shodan, Censys, ProjectDiscovery) for exposed N-central instances on typical ports (9000, 8080, 443). Cross-reference with internal asset inventory to identify rogue or unpatched deployments. Federal patch due 2026-08-07 warrants immediate triage.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central: Unauthorized Management Console Access via Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'—the attack vector. Attackers gain console access without valid credentials via non-standard endpoints. Primary detection priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central auth logs for successful logins from unexpected sources, non-standard authentication paths, or bypassed MFA. Baseline legitimate administrator patterns and alert on deviations, especially from Internet-exposed interfaces.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Asset Exposure and CVE-2026-18556 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'public-facing application' exploited in wild (CISA KEV). Organizations must enumerate all N-central instances and scan for CVE-2026-18556 with immediate remediation by federal deadline 2026-08-07.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external-facing networks for N-able N-central services. Cross-reference against inventory to identify unauthorized instances. Run CVE-2026-18556 scanner checks and enforce patch compliance against 2026-08-07 SLA.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomaly Detection: Alternate Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly leverages 'alternate path or channel' for bypass. Detection must specifically target non-standard authentication endpoints and API routes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on auth attempts to non-standard N-central paths (backup endpoints, debug URLs, undocumented routes). Correlate failed auth spikes with successes, indicating brute-force or bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Post-Compromise Behavioral Baseline
suggestion.rationale: If authentication bypassed, post-compromise actions diverge from legitimate administrator behavior. Behavioral anomalies provide best post-compromise detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline N-central admin activities (login times, task patterns, source IPs). Alert on deviations: new accounts, credential exports, policy changes, off-hours access, unexpected geolocation, bulk config modifications.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18556 Patch Compliance Tracking and Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with active exploitation and federal remediation deadline 2026-08-07. Continuous scanning and compliance tracking against deadline is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run continuous scans for CVE-2026-18556 across all N-central instances. Flag systems remaining vulnerable past 48-72 hour SLA. Generate daily remediation tracking reports targeting federal deadline.

suggestion.title: npm postinstall script execution with suspicious outbound network
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm 'automatically spread across software ecosystems by republishing malicious updates'—indicates execution phase occurs during package install and immediately connects to C2 for credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm/node processes spawning command-line interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash) during postinstall script execution, followed by network connections to non-Microsoft infrastructure. Flag processes with parents matching *npm.cmd, *npx.cmd, or node.exe launching interpreters within 2 seconds of package installation.

suggestion.title: Repeated npm package republishing from single account in short timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'automatically republished malicious updates'—indicates attacker used compromised npm accounts to push multiple package versions in rapid succession across 400+ packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query npm registry access logs and artifact repositories for single authentication token publishing 10+ package versions within 1-hour windows. Flag accounts with unusual geographic origin changes or publishing packages outside their historical maintenance scope.

suggestion.title: Credential file access during npm package post-install execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing worm'—worm must enumerate and access credential stores (.ssh, .aws, .docker, .npmrc, browser profiles) during postinstall phase before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or child processes (spawned by postinstall scripts) accessing paths matching *\.ssh, *\.aws, *\.npmrc, *\.docker, %APPDATA%\npm, or browser credential databases. Exclude legitimate package operations via allowlist of known auth libraries.

suggestion.title: Self-propagating worm dependency injection pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes worm 'self-propagating'—suggests malicious package modifies package.json or publishes new versions that include itself as a dependency, or spreads to other packages via publish-time injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm packages that introduce unexpected new dependencies or versions mid-lifecycle. Flag package.json modifications that add dependencies post-publish or package manifests that differ between registry metadata and installed artifacts. Cross-reference publishing accounts for coordinated changes.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of environment variables and secrets to external C2
suggestion.rationale: Worm steals credentials and must transmit them; article specifies credential exfiltration to attacker infrastructure outside npm ecosystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node.exe or npm-spawned processes with DNS/HTTP requests to non-npm infrastructure during package operations. Flag payloads containing common credential patterns (AWS_SECRET, github token prefix, API key patterns, JWT structures). Baseline C2 infrastructure against known attacker IOCs.

suggestion.title: Spoofed sender accepted despite SPF/DMARC failure via enterprise whitelist
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Although the messages originated from an unknown IONOS mail server, failed SPF and DMARC checks, and had no DKIM signature, they were still accepted by the receiving systems because RingCentral was whitelisted.' This is defense evasion via trusted relationship abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with failed SPF/DMARC validation that originate from non-whitelisted infrastructure but are forwarded by whitelisted domains. Track sender mismatch (From header ≠ Return-Path) combined with whitelist bypass. Baseline legitimate RingCentral forwarding paths.

suggestion.title: MFA-approved sign-ins from VPS/commercial VPN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the attacker replayed Microsoft 365 authentication tokens from VPS and commercial VPN infrastructure to access the compromised accounts.' This is post-compromise token replay.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Microsoft 365 sign-in events with valid MFA approval originating from known VPS providers (AWS, Azure, DigitalOcean) or commercial VPN services. Correlate MFA approval timestamp with phishing click timestamp. Alert if same token used from multiple geolocations within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious post-compromise Microsoft Graph enumeration of O365 resources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enumerated Outlook mailboxes, Teams conversations, SharePoint sites, OneDrive files, contacts, calendars, and registered applications through Microsoft Graph, with access persisting for more than two weeks.' This is discovery and collection via GraphAPI.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential Microsoft Graph API calls to /me/mailfolders, /me/messages, /me/chats, /me/drive, /me/registeredDevices within 1-hour window. Flag accounts showing GraphAPI activity from VPS/VPN IPs not seen in baseline. Alert on app-based GraphAPI access from non-standard OAuth applications.

suggestion.title: Device-code phishing flow targeting Microsoft 365 with MFA bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states phishing page routed victims 'through a Microsoft adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing flow that captured an MFA-approved authentication token or through a device-code phishing flow.' Device-code abuse is T1187.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device-code flow (oauth2/devicecode endpoint) from non-enterprise IP ranges or suspicious ASNs. Flag device-code MFA approval followed by token issuance within 2 minutes. Detect OAuth consent grants to unusual app IDs immediately after device-code flows. Monitor for user device-code approval events followed by unrelated resource access.

suggestion.title: Prolonged post-compromise account access and persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'access persisting for more than two weeks in some cases.' This indicates undetected persistence despite MFA compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in patterns showing continuous or near-continuous access from phishing-sourced IPs spanning >7 days without corresponding user MFA approval events. Alert on OAuth refresh token reuse across 14+ days from static IP/VPN. Flag accounts with active GraphAPI usage but no interactive user sessions in same period.

suggestion.title: Tenant-specific phishing page serving and MFA token interception
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Microsoft 365 phishing page with tenant-specific branding.' This indicates real-time tenant detection and dynamic page generation typical of AiTM attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries for spoofed Microsoft 365 endpoints (login.microsoftonline.com redirects, mail.office365.com variants). Flag HTTP CONNECT events to phishing infrastructure IPs with certificate CN mismatch. Correlate risky sign-in events (impossible travel, anomalous token claims) with proxy logs showing preceding phishing page visits.

suggestion.title: Flowise: Stolen OAuth token usage against downstream service
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'enables token theft for any connected service' but provides no detection for the final exploitation phase. The kill chain includes lateral movement via stolen tokens: 'It decrypts the stored credential (containing clientId, clientSecret, refresh_token), sends a refresh request to the configured OAuth provider, and returns the new access_token directly.' Missing: detection of those stolen tokens being used to call downstream APIs (Slack, Google, GitHub, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After token theft from Flowise, attacker uses stolen access_token to call downstream OAuth service APIs. Detect by: (1) unusual geographic/IP origin for API calls to integrated services post-refresh, (2) API calls to rare/never-before-called downstream services shortly after Flowise endpoint probing, (3) downstream service grants or data exfiltration triggered by unfamiliar OAuth2 bearer tokens.

suggestion.title: Flowise: Stored OAuth credential decryption or export
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability works because Flowise 'decrypts the stored credential (containing clientId, clientSecret, refresh_token).' This is T1555 (Credentials from Password Store) but no detection covers the decryption/access of the credential store itself. Missing: host-level detection of Flowise accessing its own credential database or exporting credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Flowise application process for: (1) reading credential database files at high frequency, (2) env var exports of decrypted OAuth secrets, (3) file writes to temp directories containing credential material, (4) unusual database queries against credential storage tables.

suggestion.title: Flowise: Unauthenticated endpoint discovery and probing
suggestion.rationale: Before exploiting the token-refresh endpoint, an attacker must discover the Flowise instance and enumerate credentialIds. This is discovery/reconnaissance (T1526, T1087). Missing: detection of probing attempts that come before the actual token-refresh exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance phase: (1) repeated 404s or status-200 responses to common Flowise paths (/api/v1/oauth2-credential*, /api/v1/credentials*), (2) sequential attempts to guess credentialIds before first successful refresh (GET requests or OPTIONS to the endpoint), (3) comparison between failed token-refresh attempts and successful ones in same source IP within short window.

suggestion.title: CSV file upload with prompt injection payload markers
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'A prompt injection sent to a chatflow using a CSV Agent node' but no detection exists for malicious CSV content itself. Requires inspection of uploaded files for jailbreak/injection markers before execution reaches Python validator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Flowise-served file uploads to /api/v1/prediction or chat endpoints. Scan CSV content for prompt-injection keywords: 'exec','system','import','__','subprocess','os.','eval(','lambda', Python string literals with shell syntax, SQL injection markers. Correlate with subsequent Python code validation rejections (UC_6_4) or shell spawning (UC_6_2).

suggestion.title: Flowise API endpoint enumeration or fuzz attempts targeting /api/v1/prediction
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) but current hunts only detect high-volume POSTs, not reconnaissance. Attackers probe /api/v1/prediction variants, parameter names, or HTTP methods before payload submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of 404/405 responses to /api/v1/prediction* endpoint, followed by successful POST. Look for User-Agent consistency (single tool), rapid requests (sub-second intervals), or parameter fuzzing patterns (?agent=, ?csv=, ?model=) that precede exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Flowise-spawned Python process with network egress and env-file access in same session
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_5 detects file access independently; needs correlation rule linking file access to network connections in same parent-child lineage. Article mentions exfiltration (T1041) over C2 but no detection connects credential access to data ex-filtration in time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Flowise-parented Python process reading .env or database.sqlite (within 30s) with outbound network connections to non-standard ports or known C2 domains. Flag if egress IP is not in allowlist (e.g., API provider subnets, software repos).

suggestion.title: Flowise database (database.sqlite) file access from web-tier child processes
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_5 mentions database.sqlite but no dedicated detection. RCE child processes should not directly access SQLite—should go through Flowise service. Direct database file access from shell spawned by web request is high-confidence post-RCE indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process (shell, Python, curl, sqlite3) spawned by node/flowise process accessing database.sqlite file directly (not via TCP port 8080 or 3000). Correlate file open/read events with process lineage confirming web-initiated parent.

suggestion.title: Rapid successive Python code validation rejections from same source IP + chatflow ID
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_4 detects rejections but no context on source or pattern. Article describes blocklist bypass (T1027) as iterative: attacker tries many prompt-injection obfuscation variations, each rejected. Clustering rejections per source/chatflow reveals attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Group Flowise security rejection logs by (source IP, chatflow ID, 5m time window). Flag if same source generates ≥5 rejections in 5 minutes, indicating iterative bypass attempts rather than accidental user error.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Ransomware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'multi-stage attack' with execution to detection in 129 seconds. No process execution or command-line UCs despite clear attack progression requiring immediate execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect obfuscated command-line execution chains, LOLBIN abuse (certutil, bitsadmin, wmic), or suspicious process spawning that precedes rapid file system I/O or network beaconing typical of ransomware initialization.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Deployment Blocked
suggestion.rationale: Description states attack was stopped 'before the payload could persist'—persistence mechanisms were actively deployed and detectable. Pipeline generated zero persistence-phase UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to HKLM/HKCU Run keys, Startup folders, and scheduled task creation with suspicious binaries or paths; flag service/WMI event subscription modifications deployed by ransomware for reboot persistence.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payload Deployment & Encryption Prevention
suggestion.rationale: Article is fundamentally about ransomware threat; description notes payload blocked from deployment. No impact-phase UCs despite clear encryption/destruction activity to detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass file writes with suspicious extensions, Volume Shadow Copy deletion (vssadmin, wbadmin), boot configuration modifications, or crypto-tool process signatures exhibiting rapid file enumeration and high I/O to user/shared directories.

suggestion.title: AnySign4PC execution from non-standard paths (temp/appdata/downloads)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states backdoors installed 'without prompts'—implies sideloaded, compromised binary executed outside Program Files. This execution context is a hallmark of supply-chain compromise and is not detected by empty pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag AnySign4PC process execution from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Downloads, or user temp directories. Validate digital signature and compare hash against known good builds. Cross-reference with recent access to Korean .kr domains in proxy logs.

suggestion.title: Unexpected child processes or DLL loads from AnySign4PC
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor delivery 'without prompts' suggests AnySign4PC spawns malware or loads malicious DLLs. Standard application behavior does not include cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe children.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes created by AnySign4PC or variants spawning LOLBins, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or regsvcs.exe. Monitor for unsigned or suspicious DLL loads within AnySign4PC process space.

suggestion.title: Network beaconing from AnySign4PC to Korean C2
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify C2 infrastructure but backdoor installation implies command-and-control channels. No UC captures anomalous outbound traffic from the compromised application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and outbound HTTPS/TCP connections originating from AnySign4PC process. Flag callbacks to Korean ASNs, recently-registered domains, or IPs hosting known malware. Alert on periodic beaconing intervals.

suggestion.title: Access to hacked Korean government/enterprise sites + AnySign4PC download correlation
suggestion.rationale: Initial-access vector: 'hacked Korean sites'. Article emphasizes this supply-chain entry point. Defenders must detect the moment users visit compromised legitimate Korean domains and correlate with subsequent binary downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish whitelist of legitimate Korean government/corporate .kr domains (banking, telecom, healthcare). Alert on first-time access from endpoints to these domains. Correlate with file downloads (especially .exe, .msi, .zip) or AnySign4PC process execution within 2-hour window on same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Registry persistence by AnySign4PC (Run keys, Services, Scheduled Tasks)
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor installation without user interaction implies persistence mechanism. Article does not specify how but scheduled tasks, run keys, or service creation are standard Korean malware patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to HKCU/HKLM \Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or Services by AnySign4PC process. Monitor for new Windows scheduled tasks executing AnySign4PC, rundll32.exe, or suspicious Korean-named binaries with system privileges.

suggestion.title: Invalid or suspicious digital signature on AnySign4PC binary
suggestion.rationale: Compromised distribution implies modified or replaced binary. Article emphasizes 'hacked Korean sites'—signature validation catches tampering. Pipeline missed signature-integrity detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AnySign4PC execution where authenticode signature fails validation (unsigned, revoked, expired), or subject name does not match legitimate publisher. Flag execution from web-cache or recently-downloaded locations with failed signature verification.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central CVE-2026-18556 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-18556 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and describes asset-exposure hunt as canonical detection. Pipeline produced no vulnerability-scanner-based detection despite this explicit requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scanner logs and CMDB for systems flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-18556 (N-able N-central). Cross-reference patch-management records to identify systems without 2026-08-07 federal remediation deadline applied. Prioritize public-facing N-central instances (RMM management consoles).

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel.' Pipeline omitted detection for suspicious authentication patterns or unconventional N-central login paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to N-able N-central management consoles for requests to non-standard authentication endpoints, unusual URI patterns, or direct administrative function calls bypassing normal login flows. Correlate with failed-then-successful authentication sequences or unauthenticated API calls to privileged functions.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Unauthorized Access and Session Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass results in valid account compromise; pipeline did not model post-bypass access patterns or RMM lateral-movement activity expected after N-central compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After N-able N-central compromise, look for unusual process execution initiated from N-central agent processes (e.g., spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or script interpreters). Monitor for lateral-movement network connections from N-central management console to endpoints not in baseline RMM management patterns. Flag sessions with mismatched or missing authentication event logs.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Federal Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due-date of 2026-08-07, creating regulatory compliance requirement. Pipeline did not generate compliance-tracking or deadline-accountability detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track remediation progress for CVE-2026-18556 across all N-able N-central instances with known federal reporting obligations. Generate daily inventory of unpatched systems, identify root-cause delays (blocked patches, incompatibility holds), and escalate systems still vulnerable 24-48 hours before 2026-08-07 deadline.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Beaconing and Command Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: RMM (Remote Monitoring & Management) software is a high-value persistence mechanism for adversaries; active KEV status suggests widespread exploitation risk. Pipeline omitted detection for suspicious RMM agent behavior or command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from N-able N-central agents to non-whitelist IP ranges, non-standard ports, or infrastructure outside typical vendor update/licensing CDNs. Flag execution of scripts or binaries staged through RMM console that deviate from vendor-signed software. Correlate command execution timing with authentication-bypass exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: N-central authentication bypass detection (alternate path)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' — pipeline must detect successful N-central logins that bypass normal credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful N-central authentication events lacking corresponding credential validation steps, or logins from unexpected paths/source IPs. Monitor N-central session creation without prior explicit authentication request.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18556 asset inventory and patch compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status and federal patch deadline (2026-08-07) require scanner coverage. Article names product and vendor explicitly for IOC matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scans for N-able N-central installations below patched version threshold. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed instances. Alert for all unpatched systems past federal due date.

suggestion.title: N-central lateral movement post-auth bypass
suggestion.rationale: N-central is a management/remote-access tool; successful auth bypass grants attacker foothold to pivot to managed endpoints. Article context implies lateral movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect N-central processes spawning remote execution to internal infrastructure outside maintenance windows: RPC, SSH, WinRM, or psexec from ncentral.exe parent. Correlate with abnormal N-central API usage.

suggestion.title: N-central API abuse and command deployment
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass grants API access; attacker likely uses N-central REST/SOAP APIs to deploy commands to managed endpoints. Article implies capability to execute as authenticated N-central admin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal N-central API patterns: bulk device queries, credential/configuration changes, or mass script deployment outside scheduled maintenance. Flag token creation and bulk API call rates from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: N-central administrative account modification
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attackers often create rogue admin accounts or escalate privileges within the management tool to cement persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for account creation, role assignment, or privilege escalation within N-central management interface post-auth bypass. Flag new N-central admin accounts, especially created post-patch-deadline or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Suspicious child process execution from N-central agent
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated, attackers abuse N-central's remote execution capabilities to run arbitrary code on managed systems via ncentral.exe or agent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or suspicious executables with parent process N-central agent (ncentral.exe) outside expected deployment/patch operations. Correlate with N-central API logs confirming remote command injection.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempt — N-able N-central Alternate Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' — core attack vector that should generate hypothesis for detecting direct bypasses of login flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central web application logs (default ports 8040/8041) for POST/GET requests to authentication-related endpoints with absent or malformed credential parameters. Alert on HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences, unexpected query parameters (e.g., ?bypass=1, ?auth=0), or direct API calls to user-management endpoints that bypass the login portal entirely.

suggestion.title: Successful N-able N-central Session Post-Failed Auth Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article claims bypass 'allows for authentication bypass' — detection must correlate suspicious/failed login attempts with subsequent authenticated sessions or API calls under the same source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal N-able N-central authentication patterns (credential submission + 200 OK + session token). Flag anomalies: session tokens issued without prior credential POST, authentication success immediately following multiple 40x/50x errors from same source, or tokens granted to known-inactive user accounts.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise N-able N-central Configuration Changes & Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article warns federal agencies must patch by 2026-08-07 — implies in-the-wild exploitation for persistence/lateral movement. Once bypassed, attackers will enumerate internal assets and pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central server for outbound connections to internal IP ranges (scanning), RDP/SSH/WinRM traffic to domain controllers/servers, and unsigned executable staging in temporary directories. Alert on N-central process spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell with -NoProfile flags, or net.exe commands for user/group enumeration.

suggestion.title: Scanner Bypass: Vulnerable N-able N-central Versions Post-Patch Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check' — patch lag is endemic; vulnerability scanners may report false-negatives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management tool for N-able N-central instances and cross-reference against Build/Version numbers known-vulnerable to CVE-2026-18556 (vendor advisory will list ranges). Flag instances marked 'patched' but running unpatched build IDs, instances with 'unknown' patch status, or those not scanned within last 30 days.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Web Server HTTP Abnormalities Indicating Bypass Technique
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass techniques often generate anomalous HTTP patterns (missing headers, unexpected methods, encoding tricks) visible in access logs before successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central IIS/Apache/nginx logs for: PUT/DELETE methods on authentication endpoints, Host-header manipulation, unusual User-Agent strings (e.g., empty, curl without normal browser fields), Content-Length: 0 on POST requests to login, or HTTP/1.0 requests (legacy exploitation technique). Spike in 401/403 errors followed by 200 OK is suspicious.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Unauthorized Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'—pipeline must detect attempts to reach N-central without valid session. Detection baseline: failed auth followed by successful access from same source within short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 401/403 to N-central admin endpoints (/admin, /api/*) followed by HTTP 200 from same source IP within 60 seconds. Flag requests lacking authorization headers to sensitive paths. Baseline known admin IP ranges first to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Alternate-Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'alternate path or channel' bypass. Detect direct API requests circumventing normal login—the exact attack vector described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to N-central /api/agents, /api/admin, or undocumented debug endpoints with missing/invalid auth headers or stale session tokens. Detect referer anomalies (direct endpoint access rather than navigating through UI) and requests from sources never authenticated to N-central.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach N-central Agent Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: After bypassing authentication, attackers pivot via N-central to command managed agents for lateral movement or data collection—article emphasizes bypass but lacks post-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous bulk agent actions: mass policy deployments to agents outside change control, script execution to agent fleet, enrollment of rogue agents from out-of-band sources. Requires N-central audit log ingestion and baseline of normal administrator command patterns.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Anomalous Session Activity
suggestion.rationale: Successful bypass authentication creates sessions from untrusted or anomalous sources. Detect sessions with unusual geolocation, timing, or behavior divergent from known administrators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline N-central admin sessions by source IP, time-of-day, device fingerprint, and geography. Alert on new source IPs, off-hours access, or sessions performing atypical actions (agent queries, policy changes) outside baseline administrator behavior profile.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18556 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'CVE-2026-18556 — match against your vulnerability scanner' with federal remediation deadline 2026-08-07. Asset discovery and exposure assessment is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-18556 against asset inventory. Identify N-able N-central instances with internet exposure (confirm via firewall rules, public IP assignment).
