suggestion.title: File write/modification in development temp directories by node.exe from remote-triggered RPC
suggestion.rationale: Article's truncated section mentions arbitrary command execution; common RPC exploitation patterns include writing malicious scripts to temp, then executing them. Detection should look for suspicious file writes to /tmp, %TEMP%, .nuxt/, .vite/ from node.exe parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation or modification of executable files (.sh, .ps1, .bat, .exe) or suspicious scripts in temp/dev directories when parent process is node.exe running a dev server, especially if preceded by non-loopback network traffic.

suggestion.title: Absence of WebSocket Upgrade authentication headers on Vite HMR connection
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'no authentication: any client... can call RPC methods, with no token, handshake, or origin check'. Safe dev servers should enforce authentication (Bearer token, session cookie, Origin header validation). Absence of these headers = indicator of vulnerable configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and alert on HTTP Upgrade requests to vite-hmr where Authorization, Cookie, or restricted Origin headers are absent. Developers should require tokens or session validation. Each unauthenticated vite-hmr WebSocket is an intrusion opportunity.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Infrastructure Detection via Domain Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions '250+ ClickFix Domains' — each is a malware lure infrastructure element. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs from title alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP requests to known ClickFix domains. Cross-reference with user-agent patterns typical of automated fingerprinting clients (headless browsers, curl/wget variants). Correlate with subsequent file downloads to identify payload delivery chain.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Delivery via Browser Fingerprinting Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'browser fingerprinting to hide macOS malware lures' — attackers fingerprint browsers to evade detection logic. Missing defense-evasion detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests with excessive or suspicious User-Agent reuse, Canvas fingerprinting JavaScript payloads (WebGL, font enumeration, hardware detect), and WebRTC IP leak probes. Flag landing pages that serve different payloads based on browser/OS profile.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Binary Download from ClickFix Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article targets macOS systems with malware delivery via these fake-fix domains. No detection for platform-specific payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macOS .dmg, .app, or .pkg downloads from known ClickFix domains. Flag subsequent execution of unsigned binaries or installers from user download folders. Correlate with persistence mechanisms (LaunchAgent, LaunchDaemon creation).

suggestion.title: Fake Browser/OS Update Lure Page Detection
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix historically impersonates OS/browser update dialogs. Article implies this social-engineering vector but pipeline ignored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTML content on suspicious domains mimicking macOS System Preferences, Safari, Chrome, or Firefox update pages. Look for JavaScript that triggers fake dialogs or redirects based on system fingerprint. Cross-reference with browser history from infected hosts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous JavaScript Fingerprinting Script Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core obfuscation technique: 'browser fingerprinting to hide' malware delivery. No detection for fingerprinting JavaScript payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify JavaScript performing Canvas fingerprinting, WebGL capability detection, Font enumeration, Plugin detection, or IP leak attempts (WebRTC). Flag pages that modify payload or content based on fingerprint results.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT API Abuse for Fraud Template Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'ChatGPT Across Multiple Fraud Schemes' — pipeline surfaced zero detection logic for LLM API misuse. This is a primary attack vector the article describes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenAI API endpoints for anomalous query patterns: bulk prompt submissions requesting phishing templates, credential harvesting scripts, or social engineering scenarios; correlate API keys with known threat infrastructure; flag high-volume API requests from Tor exit nodes or bulletproof hosters.

suggestion.title: Poipet Network Domain and Infrastructure IOC Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output shows zero IOCs. Article names 'Poipet Scam Network' — should extract or correlate C2 domains, phishing hosting, money mule infrastructure, and registrant identities associated with this group.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Collect Poipet network IOCs from OpenAI's disruption notice or law enforcement disclosures; build YARA rules for lookalike domains (currency exchange, payment gateway impostors); flag DNS resolutions to known Poipet infrastructure; correlate hosting provider and registrant patterns across related fraud domains.

suggestion.title: Phishing and Social Engineering Email Detection — Poipet Actor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Scam networks initiate via phishing/BEC; article describes 'multiple fraud schemes' but pipeline generated no email-based detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails from Poipet-attributed senders or domains; detect lookalike domains spoofing financial institutions, OpenAI support, or payment processors; identify social engineering text patterns (urgency, authority exploitation, fake verification requests); correlate malicious URLs in emails against known Poipet infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Business Email Compromise — Money Transfer Fraud Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Poipet scams historically exploit victims for financial transfer; no detection UC proposed for BEC-style wire instruction manipulation or payment diversion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with sudden wire instruction changes, account number modifications, or payment requests to new beneficiaries; flag subject-line urgency markers (URGENT, VERIFY IMMEDIATELY); detect replies to legitimate business threads with payment-compromise content; correlate sender modification with external domain patterns.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Public Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'public-facing application' and 'unauthenticated remote code execution' as the attack posture; asset exposure is the first-hop entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for TeamCity instances (default ports 8111, 9000) resolvable from external IP space without egress-only restrictions. Cross-reference internet-facing scan telemetry against vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-63077 presence.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Deserialization Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'agent polling protocol' as the attack surface and 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the flaw—payloads exploit this specific path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints for serialized Java object markers (0xaced, base64-encoded gadget chains). Alert on requests lacking authentication headers combined with binary payload inspection.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Post-Exploitation Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution'; execution phase follows successful deserialization exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent is TeamCity Java process but initiating user context is SYSTEM or unexpected service account. Correlate with absence of corresponding authenticated API call in TeamCity audit logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-08-08; scanner telemetry is authoritative control for this flaw class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner results for 'CVE-2026-63077' flagged on TeamCity instances. Priority on assets with last patch date before 2026-08-01. Validate version against JetBrains advisory to confirm vulnerability applicability.

suggestion.title: Agent Registration Without Authentication Context
suggestion.rationale: Agent polling protocol requires authentication; absence of credentials in registration events signals exploitation attempt per article's 'unauthenticated' requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TeamCity agent registration or polling requests (to /polling endpoint or similar) that lack API token, JWT, or Basic auth headers. Correlate timing with inbound RCE process spawning if available.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Exception / Crash Loops in TeamCity Logs
suggestion.rationale: Failed exploitation attempts will often trigger Java deserialization errors; successful attempts are silent but precede RCE execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt TeamCity logs for 'InvalidClassException', 'ClassNotFoundException', 'gadget', or serialization-related stack traces in agent polling handler. Combine with network-level evidence of inbound craft payloads to separate exploit attempts from legitimate errors.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Public-Facing Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' and JetBrains TeamCity instances can be exposed internet-wide. Canonical asset-exposure hunt required to identify instances needing emergency patching by federal due date 2026-08-08.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP/HTTPS traffic to TeamCity default ports (8080, 8443) from public IP space. Cross-reference with known internal infrastructure to isolate unmanaged/rogue TeamCity instances. Escalate for immediate vulnerability assessment.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability manifests 'via the agent polling protocol'. Direct monitoring of this protocol is required; generic CVE scanning misses live attacks against unpatched builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling protocol (port 9090 or HTTP-tunneled) for Java serialization gadget-chain signatures, suspicious object deserialization markers, and unauthenticated connection success. Alert on any payload delivered without valid session token or agent certificate.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Attack Detection in TeamCity Process
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause is 'deserialization of untrusted data'. Detect the attack vector itself independent of CVE-specific IOCs to catch variants and zero-days using same attack class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process spawning from TeamCity JVM (java.exe with -Dteamcity parameters) where parent process has no authenticated session in logs. Focus on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned with System privileges from TeamCity service account.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Command Execution on TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability is 'unauthenticated' — no credentials required. Detection must focus on command execution without legitimate auth artifacts to isolate exploitation from legitimate use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed or missing authentication logs with successful process creation from TeamCity JVM. Alert on batch/shell commands executed in TeamCity context that lack corresponding API token, session cookie, or SSH key validation events.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Discovery from Compromised TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Following RCE via deserialization, adversary typically executes reconnaissance. Article states unauthenticated code execution possible, implying attacker gains arbitrary command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration commands (dir, ls, Get-ChildItem), system info gathering (systeminfo, uname -a), and AD discovery (Get-ADComputer, net group) spawned from TeamCity service account with no corresponding legitimate build job or admin activity in audit logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-63077 by name in CISA KEV with explicit patch deadline. Vulnerability scanner feeds must include this CVE to detect affected builds and prioritize remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-63077 matches against all TeamCity instances. Cross-reference with patch-date telemetry to identify instances still running vulnerable versions past federal deadline 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Scanner Detection and Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'CVE-2026-63077 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends asset-exposure hunt templated from _TEMPLATES.md. Pipeline failed to generate any scanner-based detection or asset query.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-63077 matches on JetBrains TeamCity instances. Cross-reference scan findings with asset inventory, prioritize internet-facing systems, and correlate patch dates against scan timestamps. Alert on any unpatched instances after 2026-08-08 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Unauthenticated Agent Polling Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector as 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' This specific protocol-level attack surface requires dedicated network detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (typically /update, /api/agents paths) originating from external/untrusted sources without valid session tokens. Baseline legitimate agent communication from known IP ranges and alert on deviations. Flag requests with unusual payload sizes or serialized object signatures.

suggestion.title: RCE Execution Detection from TeamCity Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in command execution. Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' — must detect the execution phase, not just initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes spawned from TeamCity application processes (java.exe, tomcat, catalina). Look for unexpected shells, reconnaissance tools, or reverse shells executed in TeamCity service context. Baseline normal CI/CD activities to minimize FP.

suggestion.title: Serialized Java Object Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism is 'deserialization of untrusted data' — this requires detection of malicious serialized object payloads in network traffic to agent polling endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Java serialization magic bytes (ac ed 05 00) or base64-encoded serialized objects in HTTP POST bodies to TeamCity endpoints. Correlate with known ysoserial gadget chains or exploit signatures. High-FP risk if legitimate agents serialize — require whitelist of authorized agent IPs.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Rapid Multi-Instance Exploitation Scanning
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation. Attackers typically scan and exploit multiple targets. Article severity 'crit' warrants detection of worm-like or mass-scanning patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify single source IPs making repeated exploitation attempts across multiple internal TeamCity instances within short time window. Flag requests to /update or agent endpoints from IPs with no legitimate business context. Correlate with known Shodan/Censys queries for exposed TeamCity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV status: observed exploited in the wild, and requires substitution into standard asset-exposure template hunts. Pipeline failed to generate even baseline vulnerability detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner results and endpoint telemetry for presence of CVE-2026-63077 (JetBrains TeamCity deserialization RCE). Alert on any TeamCity instance versions prior to patched release date 2026-08-08 exposed to network or internet-facing boundaries.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' Pipeline failed to extract this protocol-level exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (typically /agentservice/* paths). Flag requests with serialized Java object payloads or suspicious POST/GET parameters from internet-sourced IPs.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Gadget Chain Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism explicitly stated as 'deserialization of untrusted data.' Standard post-exploitation detection missing for common Java gadget chains (ysoserial payloads, log4j, commons-collections).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search TeamCity server logs and network captures for serialized Java object patterns, base64-encoded payloads, and markers of common gadget chains. Monitor for unexpected process spawning (java.lang.Runtime.exec, powershell.exe, bash) as child of TeamCity agent processes post-deserialization.

suggestion.title: Exposed Public-Facing TeamCity Instance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' vulnerability and CISA KEV indicates active exploitation against exposed assets. Article directs readers to standard asset-exposure hunt templates but pipeline generated zero reconnaissance/exposure UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory hunt: identify all TeamCity instances (default ports 8111, 8112, agent 9090) reachable from internet boundary or untrusted network segments. Cross-reference with patch inventory to flag unpatched versions as of CVE-2026-63077 disclosure date.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' but pipeline failed to establish post-exploitation detection. Expected follow-on behavior: command execution, process spawning, lateral movement setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, wget, curl) originating from TeamCity agent service (typically running as 'teamcity' or SYSTEM user). Alert on connections to external C2 infrastructure or lateral movement attempts (SMB, RDP, SSH) immediately following agent polling endpoints access.

suggestion.title: Federal Remediation Deadline Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08' and emphasizes CISA KEV patch lag as 'silent killer.' Pipeline should have generated compliance-linked alert for regulatory/audit preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated compliance alerting: flag any unpatched TeamCity instances still present in production on or after 2026-08-08. Generate incident for federal audit purposes if instances remain vulnerable beyond due date.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Public-Facing Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unauthenticated remote code execution' against public instances: '[vulnerability] could allow unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'. Asset exposure is the foundation of defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally accessible TeamCity instances on default ports (8111, 8112). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-63077 positives. Flag any TeamCity versions released before 2026-08-08 patch date without documented remediation.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface explicitly named: 'via the agent polling protocol'. Deserialization exploits produce detectable protocol violations, malformed payloads, or error cascades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoints for serialized Java objects, deserialization exceptions, or protocol framing errors. Alert on unauthenticated requests to agent-register, agent-status, or build-config endpoints. Flag payloads exceeding normal size thresholds.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms RCE outcome: 'allow unauthenticated remote code execution'. Execution detection captures in-flight compromise even after initial foothold succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity parent process (java.exe running as service) for unexpected child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or process injection events. Alert on reverse shell patterns or network connections from TeamCity process context to external IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV scope: federal due date 2026-08-08 and 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Continuous compliance reporting is required for auditor queries and risk ranking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily scan for unpatched TeamCity versions matching CVE-2026-63077 signature. Cross-check patch deployment logs. Flag instances where scanner reports vulnerable but patch logs show no remediation attempt. Alert 7 days before federal deadline for compliance backlog.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: Core requirement for exploitation: 'unauthenticated' access. Anomalous administrative endpoint access without valid session tokens indicates exploitation or reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to /admin, /agent, /build, /plugins endpoints returning 401/403 from external IPs. Flag multiple sequential failed authentications. Alert on 200 responses to sensitive endpoints without preceding valid login session.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE is 'unauthenticated via the agent polling protocol.' Must identify exposed instances before exploitation; asset-exposure hunt template explicitly referenced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TeamCity instances (default TCP 8111 server, 8113 agents) accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against patch inventory for 2026-08-08 compliance. Flag instances responding to agent polling with unpatched build signatures.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Deserialization Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly identified as 'deserialization of untrusted data via the agent polling protocol'—behavioral signature detectable via Java exception logs and protocol-level anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity server/agent logs for ClassNotFoundException, BadClassDefinition, StreamCorruptedException during agent polling handshakes. Flag payloads to agent polls exceeding baseline size or containing serialized gadget-chain indicators (commons-collections, JNDI, groovy). Correlate with unexpected child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Command Execution from TeamCity Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in 'unauthenticated remote code execution'—need detection of malicious command execution spawned in TeamCity agent JVM context post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes under TeamCity agent JVM (java.exe contexts) spawning shells (cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/bash), network utilities (curl, wget, nc), or reverse shells. Baseline legitimate TeamCity build processes and flag off-policy execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance Pre-Due-Date
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and 'Federal due-date dates match timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors.' Hard stop 2026-08-08; proactive verification required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all TeamCity instances (server + agents). Confirm build version ≥ patched version by 2026-08-08. Flag instances on pre-fix builds; cross-check CISA KEV and vendor release notes to confirm patch availability and application.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via agent polling protocol.' Detection of externally accessible TeamCity instances is the canonical initial-access hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TeamCity instances (default ports 8111, agent polling 9000) responding to unauthenticated external connection attempts. Track inbound traffic to these ports from untrusted networks; flag any successful handshakes without pre-auth checks.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface explicitly identified: 'agent polling protocol.' Need detection for protocol-level exploitation attempts, not just network exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent polling protocol traffic (typically port 9000, custom headers) for unauthenticated requests followed by serialized payload transmission. Baseline legitimate build-agent handshakes; alert on deviations or payloads from non-registered agents.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Deserialization RCE Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly: 'deserialization of untrusted data.' Post-exploitation detection of actual command execution resulting from unsafe deserialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity agents or server instances (java.exe with atypical command lines). Flag deserialization exceptions in TeamCity logs followed by process creation. Look for base64-encoded payloads in polling protocol traffic.

suggestion.title: TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal due date 2026-08-08. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—detection must include asset inventory cross-reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-63077 on all TeamCity instances. Cross-reference patch date against installation date to identify systems where patch lag > 7 days. Escalate unpatched public-facing instances as critical.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Flow Approved by Non-Initiating User
suggestion.rationale: Device code phishing tricks users into approving codes they did not request. Article premise ('device code phishing…fastest-growing') implies attackers trick users into approving—detection should flag approval from different user agent, IP, or session than code requester.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OAuth device-code-flow approval events where the approver's geo, device, or user-agent differs significantly from the device-code requester. Flag rapid sequences of device-code generation followed by approval from a different principal or cross-tenant approval patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Device Code Generation Without Completion
suggestion.rationale: Phishing reconnaissance or failed campaign attempts would show high volumes of device codes generated but never approved. Article implies multi-target phishing—bulk generation is a hallmark.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline device code generation rate per app/principal; alert on >200% spike or >N codes generated in <M minutes by one app. Correlate with low approval ratio (e.g., <5% of generated codes result in approval) to surface reconnaissance or failed phishing attempts.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Containing Device Code or Device Login Instructions
suggestion.rationale: Device code phishing campaigns deliver emails with device codes or instructions to visit device.microsoft.com and approve. Article title signals this is primary delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing 8–12 alphanumeric device-code patterns, URLs to 'device.microsoft.com' or 'microsoft.com/devicelogin', or instructions to 'approve authentication code' without legitimate context. High confidence: messages impersonating Microsoft or claiming urgent security action.

suggestion.title: Device Code Token Exchange from Suspicious IP or Geo
suggestion.rationale: Once user approves device code, attacker exchanges it for access/refresh tokens. Detecting token exchange from attacker-controlled infrastructure (VPN, datacenter, foreign geo) marks credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor device-code token-exchange events for IP reputation hits, datacenter IPs, VPN footprints, or geo/time anomalies (e.g., exchange from China when user is in US, within seconds of code approval). Cross-reference successful exchanges with subsequent user impersonation or O365/cloud resource access.

suggestion.title: Service Principal Generating Device Codes for User Sign-In
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate device flows are app→user (user approves app's code). Attacking SPs generating device codes targeting human users is anomalous and may indicate OAuth app compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline device-code generation by service principals; alert if an SP known only for app-to-app flows or non-OAuth workloads suddenly initiates user-facing device flows. Flag SPs generating codes that receive approvals from external tenants or high-risk user populations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Device Code Client Metadata (User-Agent, Locale)
suggestion.rationale: Device code approvals arrive via official Microsoft apps with stable UAs and metadata. Spoofed or unusual client claims (e.g., curl, Python, non-standard clients) during approval indicate phishing attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Whitelist expected user-agents and client metadata for device-code flows per app. Alert on approvals with unrecognized User-Agent (e.g., curl, wget, custom scripts), mismatched client claims, or claims for deprecated/sunset Microsoft clients.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Deserialization Payload Detection

suggestion.title: TeamCity Patch Compliance and Inventory Hunt

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Communication Anomaly Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Gap Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Federal agencies required to patch by 2026-08-08. Pipeline should generate hunt for unpatched TeamCity instances across the fleet.

Flag any exposures on the internet-facing perimeter as critical.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Reconnaissance

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected inbound traffic to TeamCity agent polling port (default 9000/TCP). Flag connections from non-whitelisted IP ranges or connections exceeding normal agent handshake size/pattern. Correlate with TeamCity authentication logs to confirm unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Deserialization Exploitation (RCE Execution)

suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status means 'currently being exploited.' Detection should use CVE ID (CVE-2026-63077) as primary pivot for behavioral hunting beyond patches—e.g., web access logs, IDS signatures, EDR telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query IDS/IPS sensors and EDR for signatures or yara rules tagged CVE-2026-63077. Correlate with TeamCity server source IPs, looking for attack attempts (HTTP 500 errors, Java exceptions in logs, or known exploit payloads).

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify externally reachable TeamCity instances via port scanning, certificate transparency logs, or Shodan queries. Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-63077. Prioritize instances with external agent-polling endpoints exposed.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'via the agent polling protocol' — specific attack surface requiring network-level or application-level monitoring of agent communication channel
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoints for malformed deserialization payloads, binary protocol anomalies, or exploitation signatures. Look for connection bursts to known TeamCity instances from external IPs immediately before RCE indicators.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow unauthenticated remote code execution' — after successful exploitation, attacker achieves execution within TeamCity process context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) spawned by TeamCity/Tomcat JVM processes (java.exe, agent.jar) in response to unauthenticated network events. Monitor for unusual file creation in TeamCity work directories correlated with polling protocol network activity.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance for TeamCity Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV exploitation chain implies reconnaissance phase to identify exposed instances, but kill-chain reconstruction omitted discovery entirely. Attackers must first find the target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external network scanning targeting TeamCity default ports (8111, 9000) or banner-grabbing/version-enumeration attempts against Tomcat/TeamCity services. Flag scanning patterns consistent with automated vulnerability-scanning tools or Shodan-like reconnaissance for CVE-2026-63077.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Public-Facing Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' and attack surface is 'the agent polling protocol'; any exposed TeamCity instance is immediately vulnerable. Phrase: 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TeamCity instances listening on default/common ports (8111, 8112) accessible from untrusted networks. Flag any TeamCity service responding to external agent polling requests without prior authentication validation.

suggestion.title: Deserialized Java Object Detection in Agent Polling
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'deserialization of untrusted data' in the 'agent polling protocol'. Attackers send malicious serialized payloads to trigger RCE. Phrase: 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for base64/hex-encoded or binary serialized Java object patterns in TeamCity agent polling protocol traffic (typically HTTP POST requests to /agents/api/*). Look for unusual serialization gadget chains (commons-beanutils, JNDI payloads) in logs.

suggestion.title: TeamCity RCE Post-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands within TeamCity process context. Phrase: 'unauthenticated remote code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from TeamCity java.exe or tomcat.exe processes, particularly PowerShell, cmd.exe, or shell interpreters. Flag process creation with network or file I/O immediately after agent polling protocol activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance and Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and notes that 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet'. Version enumeration is critical defensive measure. Phrase: 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for TeamCity version information in HTTP responses (Server headers, /login.jsp version banners, /app/rest/version endpoints). Correlate with patch dates; flag instances claiming >patch level with actual service banners revealing older build numbers.

suggestion.title: Compromised TeamCity Agent Lateral Movement and C2
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker exploits TeamCity via agent polling, compromised agents become persistence/C2 nodes. Agent-to-controller communication is encrypted channel for command relay. Phrase: 'agent polling protocol' suggests bi-directional control channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for TeamCity agent heartbeat and polling intervals. Flag agents with abnormal request rates, large payload sizes in agent polling, or agents connecting from unexpected subnets/geographic regions. Monitor for agent-to-agent communication lateral movement.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Audit and Agent Registry Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker likely registers rogue agents or disables audit logging to hide persistence. Phrase: 'observed exploited in the wild' suggests sophisticated threat actors covering tracks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity audit logs for deletion/disabling of logging, agent registry creation with unusual names or certificates, and authentication bypass configuration changes. Alert on any modification to agent authentication settings.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Asset Exposure Hunt — TeamCity Vulnerability Scan

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol — Unauthenticated Deserialization Exploit

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling protocol traffic (default port ~9000) for unauthenticated connection handshakes followed by suspicious serialized Java payloads. Flag serialized gadget chains, command injection patterns, or oversized/malformed agent jar requests from unknown IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Web Access — Exploit Probe Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote code execution' capability; exploitation requires no credentials, enabling broad reconnaissance by threat actors before CVE-2026-63077 patch deadline.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Server — Post-Exploitation Child Process Execution (RCE)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity JVM process (java.exe w/ teamcity args) for unexpected child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, wget, curl, python. Baseline legitimate build tasks and plugin behavior. High-confidence alert if child process spawning occurs minutes after unauthenticated agent-polling traffic or web access anomalies.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawning network connections to Telegram API endpoints (api.telegram.org:443) or Telegram bot webhook servers. Correlate with process parents (cmd, powershell, python interpreters). Flag connections from non-browser processes to Telegram, especially if parent is a scheduled task or service.

suggestion.title: DeepSeek LLM API Abuse and Autonomous Payload Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Commands DeepSeek' and 'Launch Autonomous Attacks'—indicates LLM is being weaponized to generate or execute payloads. Pipeline missed this attack surface entirely.

Track LLM inference latency spikes and output sizes suggesting malicious prompt injection. Correlate Telegram inbound commands with DeepSeek API calls within 5-second windows.

suggestion.title: LLM-Spawned Process Execution Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: 'Autonomous Attacks' implies the LLM is directly executing code or commands. Standard endpoint detection may miss parent-child chains rooted in language model inference or interpretation services.

Watch for interpreter processes (powershell, cmd, bash) spawned without user interactive session or RDP logon event. Baseline legitimate LLM tool usage and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Telegram Actor Persistence and Autonomous Scheduled Execution

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled tasks created with Telegram bot IDs or tokens in the command line. Alert on Task Scheduler or cron jobs executing Python/PowerShell scripts that call Telegram API. Check registry Run keys for references to Telegram libraries or bot credentials.

suggestion.title: Chinese Threat Actor Attribution via Telegram Bot Infrastructure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Telegram bot IDs and channel identifiers against published Chinese APT infrastructure signatures. Flag Telegram accounts with Cyrillic or Chinese username patterns, account creation dates clustering around known APT campaign windows, or bot tokens published in underground forums.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack Detection: Initial Access via Messaging to LLM Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies a complete kill chain (messaging C2 → LLM command injection → autonomous execution) but pipeline segmented nothing. Requires multi-event correlation across Telegram, LLM API, and process execution layers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build a correlation rule: (1) Inbound Telegram message from suspicious bot → (2) DeepSeek API inference call with high token count or unusual parameters → (3) Process creation from interpreter parent within 10 seconds. Weight by frequency of chain and legitimacy of parent process. Baseline normal LLM usage per user/host and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebSocket handshake requests to node.exe-owned ports (typically HMR ports 5173/5174 range) with subprotocol header containing 'vite-hmr' and originating from non-local IP. Absence of Authorization or security headers in WebSocket upgrade request also indicates potential abuse.

suggestion.title: RPC method invocation on nuxt:devtools:rpc channel (launch-editor or other exploitation method)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'launch-editor RPC abuse' as the specific exploitation vector but no detection for actual RPC method calls. This is the exploitation phase and should have dedicated detection beyond process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WebSocket connection to Vite HMR port followed within <5 seconds by unexpected child process creation from node.exe (shells, LOLBins). If application-level logging available, detect 'launch-editor' RPC method calls with suspicious file paths or command payloads.

suggestion.title: Vite dev server listening on 0.0.0.0 or exposed via --host flag (attack surface exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'non-loopback' access to HMR endpoint. The root cause is server configured with --host (bind to all interfaces) rather than default localhost. Detection of this configuration is recon/persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe processes with parent command line containing '--host' flag or containing .nuxt/ directory with vite.config.js/ts that includes host:'0.0.0.0' or host:'::'. This indicates intentional or misconfigured exposure to network.

suggestion.title: Correlation: HMR port connection + rapid shell child process + no user interaction (automated attack)
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate developers might connect to HMR endpoints and spawn shells (e.g., running npm commands), but the attack is unauthenticated and can be automated. Detect the chain: inbound non-loopback connection to HMR port → node.exe spawn shell child → no interactive user session for that user at that time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequence: (1) non-loopback WebSocket connection accepted on HMR port, (2) shell spawn from node.exe parent within 2 seconds, (3) no corresponding user logon event or interactive session for that user in past 5 minutes. This rules out legitimate developer scenarios where the user is actively running commands.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent protocol requests missing auth tokens, valid agent UUIDs, or that originate from IPs outside known agent ranges. Baseline normal agent identifiers and polling patterns; alert on first-time or anomalous agent connections.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'via the agent polling protocol'—exploitation targets this specific channel. Normal polling has baseline frequency, size, and timing; detect deviations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for agent polling request size, frequency, and response time. Alert on oversized payloads, unusual polling intervals, connections from non-standard ASNs or geographic regions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match—CVE-2026-63077
suggestion.rationale: Article: Federal patch due 2026-08-08. CISA KEV entries require active compliance tracking. Standard inventory-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-63077 across all detected TeamCity instances. Track patch status against federal due date. Alert on any unpatched instances; prioritize based on internet exposure.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing - Bulk Authentication Requests from Anomalous IPs
suggestion.rationale: Device code phishing exploits OAuth 2.0 device authorization flows by tricking users into entering codes from fake auth pages. Article frames this as 'fastest-growing threat of 2026' with 6 distinct attack reasons, implying repeated abuse patterns and scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure/M365 device code authentication endpoints for: (1) multiple device codes issued to same user from different geolocations within short windows, (2) device code redemption from IP ranges with no historical org presence, (3) user entering device code after clicking external phishing link.

suggestion.title: Compromised OAuth Device Flow - Token Exfiltration via Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes device code phishing as growing threat; this targets OAuth tokens obtained through social engineering, enabling account takeover without direct password compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag device code redemptions that follow anomalous patterns: device code generated at one IP/timestamp, entered from a geographically impossible location minutes later, or from Tor/VPN exit nodes not previously associated with organization.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel Detection - Device Code Auth to Cloud Access
suggestion.rationale: If phishing succeeds and attacker obtains valid OAuth token via device code, lateral movement to cloud services becomes viable. Impossible travel on subsequent cloud activity signals account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate device code authentication event location against subsequent cloud resource access (Teams, SharePoint, Exchange) from conflicting geolocations; flag if user authenticates with device code from Location A, then accesses cloud resources from Location B at impossible speed.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass Indicator - Device Code Phishing Success Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes device code phishing as high-risk because it 'bypasses MFA' - a critical attack mechanism. Successful phishing results in legitimate authenticated sessions despite MFA policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sign-ins that complete device code flow (MFA satisfied) but originate from suspicious contexts: new device, unknown location, anomalous user-agent, or immediately after phishing link click detected in proxy/email logs.

suggestion.title: Device Code Reuse and Replay - Attacker Token Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Device codes are single-use by design, but phishing infrastructure may attempt replay or batch redemption of harvested codes across multiple accounts simultaneously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed device code redemption attempts for same code value or sequential device code patterns from same attacker infrastructure; spike in device code generation followed by high failure rates suggests phishing farm attempting code harvesting.

suggestion.title: Phishing Landing Page Hosting Detection - Device Code Redirect Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Device code phishing requires fake OAuth login pages. Monitoring for suspicious hosting patterns and redirect chains leading to OAuth endpoints can identify attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains registered recently that mimic OAuth login pages, host device code collection forms, or redirect to Microsoft/Google/Github device authorization endpoints; correlate with phishing email delivery detected via SMTP logs.

suggestion.title: Identify Exposed JetBrains TeamCity Instances (Asset-Exposure Hunt)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol' and references standard asset-exposure template. This is the primary detection required for CISA KEV remediation workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TeamCity web consoles and agent polling endpoints reachable from untrusted networks. Look for listening ports 8111/8112 or /agents/* paths accessible without prior authenticated session establishment from external ASNs.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated RCE Attempts via Agent Polling Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector described as 'unauthenticated remote code execution' — pipeline must detect exploitation attempts. Article establishes specific protocol channel (agent polling) as attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (/agents/*, /build/agents) from unauthenticated sources carrying serialized Java payloads, binary content, or unusual encoding. Correlate with subsequent process spawning on TeamCity server.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution from TeamCity Server
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability grants unauthenticated RCE; attackers will execute commands post-exploitation. Pipeline must detect execution phase consequences on compromised TeamCity host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity server processes (typically java.exe/java process) for suspicious child process spawning, script invocation, or network connections. Flag execution of utilities absent from baseline (curl, wget, certutil, etc.) spawned without legitimate build job context.

suggestion.title: Track Patch Remediation Status for CVE-2026-63077 (Federal Deadline 2026-08-08)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies hard remediation deadline; pipeline must generate compliance verification UC. CISA KEV entries carry mandatory federal agency patch timelines — auditor queries inevitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-deadline inventory sweep (after 2026-08-08): query vulnerability scanner for TeamCity instances running any version released before patch publication. Flag any remaining vulnerable installations as compliance violation and escalate for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Agent Polling Traffic Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'agent polling protocol' as exploitation channel. Legitimate polling patterns can be baselined; exploitation attempts will deviate in frequency, payload size, or source location.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate TeamCity agent polling (frequency per configured agents, expected source subnets, typical payload size). Alert on: polling from new/external IPs, unusually large payloads, polling frequency spikes, or polling to agent endpoints from non-agent source ranges.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Asset Exposure - CVE-2026-63077
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' and is CISA KEV (actively exploited). Detection prerequisite is inventory of exposed TeamCity instances. Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TeamCity web interface accessibility (default ports 8111/8112) from untrusted networks. Alert on external HTTPS connections to known TeamCity instances. Correlate with CVE-2026-63077 vulnerability scanner results to identify exposed, unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable TeamCity Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-63077 affects JetBrains TeamCity; federal patch due 2026-08-08. Article references asset-exposure template requiring version inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query running TeamCity instances for version disclosure (build number) in HTTP headers or login pages. Cross-reference against CISA/NVD patched build metadata. Flag instances on builds prior to patch release date.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack vector as 'via the agent polling protocol'—this is the network-level telemetry surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal TeamCity agent-to-server polling patterns (source IPs, request cadence, message size). Alert on polling-like protocol activity from suspicious sources, with serialized Java object payloads, or without valid agent authentication credentials.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution (T1059)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution'—once exploit succeeds, attacker gains arbitrary command execution. T1059 is the post-exploitation indicator the pipeline missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity Java process (java -jar teamcity-server.jar or agent launcher) for suspicious child process spawning, shell execution, or reverse-shell callbacks. Alert on unexpected command-line activity from TeamCity service accounts or agent runtimes.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance Hunt—TeamCity Vulnerability Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and provides explicit directive: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE: CVE-2026-63077'. Federal patch due 2026-08-08 is a hard compliance deadline for federal agencies and an audit marker for enterprise SOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for unpatched CVE-2026-63077 matches on TeamCity. Correlate against network segmentation (public/DMZ exposure). Alert if unpatched instances are externally reachable.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol—Deserialization Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'agent polling protocol' as the explicit attack surface and vulnerability as 'deserialization of untrusted data.' Exploitation requires sending malicious serialized objects. Need protocol-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity polling endpoints for suspicious payloads: Java/C# serialization magic bytes, ysoserial gadget-chain patterns, oversized payloads, or protocol-version anomalies.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Unauthenticated RCE—Post-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow unauthenticated remote code execution.' Once deserialization succeeds, attacker has code execution on TeamCity service account and will spawn tools or reverse shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child process creation under TeamCity service account (typically running as SYSTEM or dedicated SVC account). Look for cmd.exe, PowerShell, curl, wget, or lateral-movement tool spawning.

suggestion.title: External Exposure—Public-Facing TeamCity Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means 'observed exploited in the wild.' Implies attackers are scanning for exposed instances. Article provides 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190) as the initial vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Shodan/Censys for internet-facing TeamCity instances. Correlate results with internal asset inventory. Flag any found on untrusted networks or without expected firewall rules.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector is 'via the agent polling protocol'—this is the attack surface requiring monitoring for malicious deserialization payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoint for unusual request payloads, timing patterns, or Java deserialization gadget chain indicators. Flag connections from unexpected internal/external addresses to the agent polling port.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scan / Banner Grab Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-63077 as the exploited vulnerability. Baseline detection must confirm presence via version detection or known endpoint fingerprinting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory against TeamCity build versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-63077. Alert on successful version identification scans or HTTP responses containing TeamCity version strings indicating vulnerable builds.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Internet-Facing Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' is the attack—implies the service must be internet-facing. Precondition check is critical for risk scoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Confirm all TeamCity instances are properly segmented and not directly accessible from untrusted networks. Alert on any inbound connections from internet IP ranges to TeamCity HTTP/HTTPS ports (8080, 443 or custom).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article's end-state is 'remote code execution'—after exploitation, detect command execution or process spawning from TeamCity agent context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from TeamCity agent runtime (typically Java). Alert on unexpected process execution (cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash, wget, curl) originating from TeamCity service account or Java process.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'deserialization of untrusted data'—requires behavioral detection of gadget chain or payload signatures specific to Java deserialization attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on serialized Java object payloads in TeamCity agent polling requests. Look for known gadget chain libraries (commons-collections, spring-core) in request bodies or abnormal request sizes to the polling endpoint.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Exploitation Attempts Against TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' This is the primary attack vector and should be detected on first attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoint for POST requests with serialized Java payloads or deserialization indicators (common patterns: Base64-encoded serialized objects, JNDI string references, or protocol protocol anomalies in /agents/api requests). CISA KEV status means exploitation is active in the wild.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated' RCE, meaning the polling protocol lacks proper auth validation. Detection should flag successful polling without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful agent polling requests (HTTP 200) that lack valid TeamCity authentication headers or session cookies. Cross-reference against known legitimate agent IPs; the polling endpoint should not be reachable without auth.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from TeamCity Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful deserialization RCE will result in command execution. Article mentions RCE capability; detection must cover execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process creation from TeamCity service accounts (e.g., teamcity or java.exe/javaw.exe running under TeamCity context). Baseline legitimate build/agent processes and alert on anomalous executables (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget from TeamCity service).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised TeamCity Server
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE to a build orchestration server grants attacker access to credentials, build configs, and internal network. Article does not mention containment; lateral movement is high-risk next step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for outbound connections from TeamCity servers. Alert on unexpected SSH/RDP/WinRM connections to internal systems, especially credential stores or other build/CI systems. Monitor DNS for beaconing or C2 resolution from the server.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Build Configuration or Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: TeamCity stores CI/CD secrets, source credentials, and build pipelines. Compromised server enables credential theft for supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity credential storage directories (.buildServer/system/pluginData) and logs for unauthorized access patterns (bulk reads, export requests, config file access outside normal build ops). Alert on unusual file reads or archive creation in TeamCity directories.

suggestion.title: TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt... Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in _TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline failed to instantiate this template with CVE-2026-63077.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scanner results (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable, etc.) for CVE-2026-63077 hits on TeamCity assets. Cross-reference with patch inventory to identify unpatched instances. Generate asset list for prioritized remediation before 2026-08-08 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Malicious Agent Polling Protocol Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—this is the precise attack vector. Pipeline missed network-based detection for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent-polling protocol endpoints (port 9090 or configured agent port) for unauthenticated requests with serialized Java object payloads. Detect malformed agent polling requests that deviate from legitimate build-agent handshakes. Alert on unusual request patterns preceding RCE indicators.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Gadget Chain Execution
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism is 'deserialization of untrusted data'—classic Java gadget-chain attack. Article describes the exploit method but pipeline provided no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious Java deserialization attempts within TeamCity JVM: monitor for ObjectInputStream calls with unexpected class types, exception stack traces containing gadget-chain indicators (ysoserial chains: CommonsCollections, Spring, etc.), or memory anomalies post-deserialization.

suggestion.title: TeamCity RCE Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE via deserialization 'could allow...remote code execution'—successful exploitation results in arbitrary process execution under TeamCity context. Pipeline did not generate execution-phase process-spawning detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from TeamCity Java process (javaw.exe, java.exe) with unusual command lines, especially shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash). Flag process execution with low or no parent authority. Correlate with preceding agent-polling traffic anomalies.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Patch Compliance Verification Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08'—3-day deadline indicates urgent compliance requirement. Pipeline should generate UC to hunt unpatched instances post-deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference TeamCity instance inventory with product version database to identify instances running versions prior to patched release (specify vendor's patched version once available). Trigger alert for any unpatched TeamCity instance still online after federal due date. Generate weekly compliance report showing patch status by asset.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Attempt Failure Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is 'unauthenticated' exploitation path. Failed exploitation attempts may leave detectable signatures in TeamCity logs (serialization errors, exception stack traces, auth bypass attempts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt TeamCity application logs for exceptions matching deserialization attack signatures: ClassNotFoundException for gadget-chain classes, InvalidClassException, or unauthenticated requests to agent-polling endpoints followed by serialization errors. Aggregate failed RCE attempts by source IP to identify attacker reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—this is the explicit attack vector and should be the primary detection. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated or anomalous requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (typically port 8111, path /agent/...). Alert on connections from external/untrusted networks to exposed TeamCity instances. Baseline legitimate agent polling and detect deviations in request patterns or source IPs.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Gadget Chain Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability'—Java deserialization attacks have characteristic binary payloads and exception signatures. Pipeline did not map to T1203 or generate serialization-focused detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity application logs for Java deserialization errors (ClassNotFoundException, InvalidClassException, ClassCastException on untrusted streams). Detect suspicious ysoserial-like payloads in HTTP POST bodies to /agent endpoints. Alert on process creation (java.exe) with unusual command-line arguments or parent process anomalies following TeamCity API calls.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE Command Execution from TeamCity Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'unauthenticated remote code execution'—successful exploitation will result in command execution. Pipeline missed T1059 mapping and did not generate execution-phase hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) from TeamCity service account (typically 'teamcity' or similar). Alert on suspicious child processes of java.exe (TeamCity JVM). Look for encoded payloads, network connections, or file writes initiated by TeamCity-spawned processes post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Beaconing from Compromised TeamCity Instance
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability ('unauthenticated remote code execution') enables attacker callbacks. Pipeline did not generate C2 detection use cases or network-based follow-on indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP from TeamCity instances to external IPs (especially non-standard ports or after hours). Alert on DNS queries for newly registered or suspicious domains initiated by TeamCity processes. Detect beaconing patterns (regular intervals, consistent packet sizes) from the TeamCity host.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Match – Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries require immediate vulnerability scanning and asset inventory correlation. Pipeline did not generate the canonical asset-exposure hunt despite article providing the CVE ID and patch deadline (2026-08-08).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for hosts matching TeamCity product/version and CVE-2026-63077. Cross-reference with network exposure data (public-facing, DMZ, VPN-accessible). Prioritize remediation by patch deadline (2026-08-08) per CISA mandate. Correlate scanner alerts with authentication logs and network flows to identify active exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Authentication or Session Activity to TeamCity Web Console
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated access via polling protocol is the entry; secondary indicators would include anomalous login attempts or session hijacking post-RCE. Pipeline did not map credential access or lateral movement implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity authentication logs for failed login spikes followed by successful sessions from anomalous IPs. Detect concurrent sessions from the same user across geographically distant locations. Alert on API token creation or privilege escalation following exploitation window (correlated with CVE-2026-63077 scanning or exploitation indicators).

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot Command & Control Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Commands DeepSeek via Telegram'—indicating Telegram as the primary C2 channel. Pipeline extracted zero signal on this attack delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Telegram bot interactions and API calls from unexpected processes. Flag accounts issuing commands to LLM endpoints via Telegram bots, especially rapid-fire or automated command sequences. Correlate Telegram API traffic with execution of system commands or malware staging.

suggestion.title: LLM API Abuse for Malicious Code Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article core premise: 'DeepSeek via Telegram to Launch Autonomous Attacks'—DeepSeek (LLM) is being weaponized for attack generation. Pipeline did not flag LLM API abuse as a risk vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual API traffic to DeepSeek endpoints or similar LLM services. Flag accounts with no legitimate business use generating hundreds of API requests. Detect patterns where LLM responses are immediately executed as shell commands or scripts.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Malware Execution via LLM Orchestration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Autonomous Attacks' triggered by LLM prompts. Pipeline failed to model the attack sequence where LLM output directly triggers system-level actions without human intervention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process chains where execution events immediately follow LLM API calls with no human interaction time-gap. Flag automated deployment of malware payloads initiated by LLM-generated commands. Correlate rapid, repetitive attack attempts (possible LLM loop unrolling) with single threat source.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DeepSeek or LLM API Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article implies compromised or stolen DeepSeek API credentials used to orchestrate attacks. Pipeline extracted no credential-based IOCs or anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DeepSeek (or LLM provider) API keys in process arguments, environment variables, or network traffic. Detect API authentication from non-standard geolocations or IPs. Flag API usage spikes at off-hours or from VPN/proxy infrastructure associated with China-based threat actors.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform LLM-to-Telegram-to-Execution Attack Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multi-hop attack workflow: attacker → Telegram bot → DeepSeek → autonomous malware. Pipeline failed to reconstruct this end-to-end kill chain and associated detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create cross-event correlation that links Telegram API activity → LLM endpoint requests → subsequent process creation or file writes. Flag sequences where Telegram interactions precede suspicious LLM API calls within minutes. Monitor for attacker infrastructure (proxies, VPNs) used to hide Telegram→DeepSeek communication chains.

suggestion.title: Detect Exposed TeamCity Instances Running Vulnerable Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' — requires asset-exposure baseline detection. Article explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template but no instance-discovery UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate TeamCity instances on external/routable IPs (ports 8080, 8443). Cross-reference against known-vulnerable versions pre-2026-08-08. Flag any unauthenticated access to polling endpoints or agent registration routes.

suggestion.title: Detect Deserialization Attack Payloads in Agent Polling Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'via the agent polling protocol' as the precise attack vector. No protocol-level detection suggested despite this being the distinguishing technical detail of the exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoints for serialized Java object payloads, protocol anomalies, or requests with embedded gadget chains. Look for Base64-encoded or binary payloads in polling requests to agents endpoint.

suggestion.title: Detect Command Execution Post-Exploitation on TeamCity Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms RCE outcome ('unauthenticated remote code execution') — no post-compromise execution indicators suggested despite this being the attacker's final objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for abnormal process spawning from java.exe (TeamCity server/agent processes) — especially PowerShell, cmd.exe, or reverse shells. Monitor for TeamCity process lineage anomalies and child-process execution with low prevalence.

suggestion.title: Correlate Patch Status Against Federal Remediation Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08' — this is both an attack urgency signal and a compliance reporting requirement. No deadline-aware detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track TeamCity instance remediation against federal deadline. Flag any instance still running vulnerable version on 2026-08-09 or later as both active risk and compliance violation. Tie to patch-management SLAs.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement from TeamCity to Build Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: RCE on central build system (TeamCity) typically enables lateral movement to repositories, artifact stores, CI/CD pipelines, and developer machines. Article omits post-initial-access attacker behavior despite high-impact target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, monitor for connections from compromised TeamCity server to internal git repos, artifact repositories, build nodes, and developer workstations. Flag credential-harvesting attempts targeting build credentials or SSH keys.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Query
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2026-63077 explicitly; no vulnerability-detection logic was generated. CISA KEV entries mandate rapid asset inventory and patch status validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-63077 across JetBrains TeamCity fleet. Prioritize instances with agent polling endpoints (ports 8111, 9090) exposed to untrusted networks or public internet.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Agent Polling Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—no network-level detection for unauthorized protocol access was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (/download/buildAgentUpdateInfo, /polling paths) originating from external/untrusted IP ranges without valid agent authentication tokens or certificates.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Gadget Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is triggered via 'deserialization of untrusted data'—exploit delivery involves malicious serialized objects. No detection for gadget-chain instantiation patterns was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or oversized serialized Java objects sent to agent polling endpoints; correlate with immediate process-spawning activity from TeamCity service account. Flag ysoserial-style gadget chains (commons-collections, JNDI references) in agent protocol traffic.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Spawning from TeamCity Service
suggestion.rationale: RCE via deserialization implies child-process execution from TeamCity daemon/agent context. Article states 'remote code execution' but no post-exploitation process-hunting logic was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal process children of TeamCity service account (java.exe, teamcityd). Alert on unexpected spawning of shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash), compilers, script interpreters, or file-transfer utilities. Correlate timing with inbound exploit attempts to agent polling endpoints.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Public Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'public-facing application' and federal patch-due of 2026-08-08. No asset-inventory or network-exposure detection generated despite this being highest-priority for federal remediation timelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all TeamCity instances with open agent polling ports on external networks (Shodan, Censys, internal port scans). Flag instances reachable from untrusted CIDR ranges and cross-validate against vulnerability scanner for patch status.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Detection
