suggestion.title: Malicious Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is in 'agent polling protocol' with 'deserialization of untrusted data'—this is the attack vector. No use case captures suspicious payloads or protocol abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/request to TeamCity agent polling endpoint with serialized object payloads, especially those containing ysoserial-like gadget chains, base64 encoding of Java objects, or triggering deserialization exceptions. Flag failures and retries as exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Process Execution from TeamCity Service
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unauthenticated remote code execution' outcome, but pipeline contains no use case for process spawning, shell execution, or command-line activity under TeamCity context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, etc.) with parent process being TeamCity service/agent, or spawned from TeamCity installation directory. Unusual in most environments; baseline and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Unusual Network Egress from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: RCE implies potential C2 or data exfil; article does not exclude post-exploitation activity. Pipeline generated no lateral-movement or command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from TeamCity process (especially to non-corporate infrastructure, dynamic DNS, or known C2 IP ranges). Baseline normal TeamCity traffic (package repos, build targets) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Reverse-Shell or Interactive Shell Spawning Under TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Deserialization RCE typically leads to shell access. Article does not rule out interactive exploitation. Pipeline missed common post-RCE indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect nc, bash -i, python -c socket shells, or PowerShell reverse shells spawned by or connecting through TeamCity. Look for parent-child relationships: TeamCity → cmd/powershell/bash → nc/socat/python.

suggestion.title: Modified or Planted Files Under TeamCity Install/Work Directories
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence often involves file writes. Article's RCE capability does not exclude artifact creation. Pipeline produced no detection for file-system change.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected file creation or modification (especially .jar, .class, .sh, .ps1, .exe, .dll) in TeamCity directories (e.g., /opt/TeamCity/*, C:\TeamCity\*). Baseline and alert on suspicious extensions or non-admin writes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Root Shell Spawning on Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Zbtlink Routers Ship With Backdoor That Opens Unauthenticated Root Shells'. Core attack is shell access without credential presentation. Detection must key on root process spawning without preceding login/authentication events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for root (uid=0) or Administrator-equivalent shell (sh, bash, cmd.exe) spawning on network appliances without antecedent authentication events (telnet login, SSH key exchange, HTTP auth). On Zbtlink/Linux routers, look for unexpected /bin/sh or /bin/bash children of network daemons (telnetd, httpd, dropbear) lacking PAM/login context.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Telnet/SSH Access to Network Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Headline establishes 'unauthenticated root shells' as the vulnerability. Backdoor likely exposes telnet/SSH without valid credentials. Must detect connection attempts to router management ports (23, 22) that yield root access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to TCP/23 (telnet) or TCP/22 (SSH) on suspected Zbtlink routers, especially those establishing root shells immediately. Look for connection success followed by command execution as root without password prompts or multi-factor auth.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Backdoor Firmware Persistence Check
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is pre-loaded in shipped firmware ('Chinese-Made Zbtlink Routers Ship With Backdoor'). Backdoor is persistent across reboots. Detection must verify firmware integrity and compare against known-good checksums.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Zbtlink appliances, verify firmware version and checksum against manufacturer releases. Alert if checksum mismatches known-good, or if firmware version is known-vulnerable. Detect suspicious persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, rc.local modifications, init.d/systemd backdoors) installed at boot.

suggestion.title: Zbtlink Router Model Enumeration and Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Zbtlink as affected vendor. Detection must identify and inventory all Zbtlink devices on the network, check for internet-facing instances, and flag them for firmware patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan network for Zbtlink router MAC OUIs or device fingerprints (HTTP Server header, UPnP announcements, DHCP User-Agent). Cross-reference with shodan/censys data to identify internet-exposed instances. Flag all Zbtlink devices for firmware audit and isolation until patched.

suggestion.title: Root Shell Command Execution on Backdoored Zbtlink Device
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes that the vulnerability grants 'unauthenticated root shells.' Once shell is opened, attacker gains full device control. Detection must capture malicious commands executed as root after unauthorized access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting unauthenticated root shell open (see UC1), monitor shell command logs for suspicious patterns: network reconnaissance (ifconfig, route, iptables), credential harvesting (cat /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd), lateral movement (ssh key generation, scp), or data exfiltration (wget, curl, nc).

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Pattern: Backdoor Activation/Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Headline implies a specific trigger or exploit path to open the root shell ('Opens Unauthenticated Root Shells'). Detection should identify the attack sequence before root shell opens, to enable early blocking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If article details a specific exploit payload, HTTP request pattern, or command sequence that triggers the backdoor, detect attempts to access vulnerable HTTP endpoints, inject specific payloads, or send crafted packets that activate the shell. Baseline normal management traffic to this router and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Ransomware Deployment: Data Theft + Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stole corporate data and demanded payments in exchange for decryption keys or promises that the stolen information would not be publicly leaked' — two-stage attack (exfiltrate then encrypt) with dual-extortion threats must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ransomware encryption activity (T1486) preceded by bulk data transfers over C2 or alternative channels (T1041/T1020). Correlate file modification patterns (encryption indicators: .ransom suffix, rapid changes, entropy spikes) with network exfiltration events 24-72 hours prior.

suggestion.title: RaaS Affiliate Network Command & Control Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'affiliate website that allowed members...to manage attacks, communicate with each other, negotiate ransom demands, and distribute revenue shares' — traffic to RaaS portal infrastructure and C2 coordination must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify encrypted HTTPS traffic to known or suspected RaaS portal domains; look for periodic beaconing patterns, asymmetric data flows (small uploads, large downloads), and traffic clustering around known Ransom Cartel C2 infrastructure indicators.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mixer Payment Obfuscation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Silnikau 'transmitted ransom payments through cryptocurrency mixers to make it harder for law enforcement to trace the funds' — mixer interaction is a post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and network connections to known cryptocurrency mixer services (e.g., Tornado Cash, ChipMixer, CoinJoin interfaces). Correlate with preceding ransomware incidents or financial data theft to identify ransom laundering workflow.

suggestion.title: Initial Access Broker (IAB) Activity & Compromised Credential Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies threat actors 'supplied members with information and tools...including stolen credentials for compromised computers' — IAB credential drops and shared access repositories must be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound logins using credentials known to have been exposed or shared via underground forums; flag bulk credential uploads to attacker repositories; monitor for anomalous RDP/SSH connections from non-standard geolocations preceding ransomware deployment.

suggestion.title: Healthcare/Medical Device Targeting Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article documents August 2022 attack on 'medical technology startup developing robotic surgical technology' with 'two month' operational impact — vertical-specific targeting and extended dwell-time are indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For healthcare and medical device environments, alert on ransomware encryption activity in surgical system directories or clinical IT infrastructure; correlate with network reconnaissance of OT/medical device vlans and slowdowns in automated device control systems lasting >24 hours.

suggestion.title: REvil Code Variant / Ransomware Family Kinship Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states Ransom Cartel 'shared code similarities with the REvil ransomware encryptor' — cross-family technical correlation is actionable attribution and allows threat hunting against known REvil signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Use yara/sigma rules built for REvil encryption routines and privilege escalation code; apply to Ransom Cartel samples to identify shared code sections. Hunt for process injection (T1134) and DLL sideloading (T1574.002) patterns consistent with REvil family obfuscation techniques noted as absent in Ransom Cartel (suggesting insider authorship).

suggestion.title: ClickFix Domain Access via DNS or HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'over 250 ClickFix domains use browser fingerprinting'—minimum viable detection is DNS/HTTP logging to known malicious domains. Pipeline provided zero domain IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS requests or HTTP connections to known ClickFix infrastructure domains. Alert on user browsing to malicious domains, particularly if followed by file download or process execution events on macOS systems.

suggestion.title: Browser Fingerprinting JavaScript Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'browser fingerprinting to hide malware lures'—requires detection of Canvas API, WebGL, User-Agent collection, or similar fingerprinting patterns in JavaScript payloads or HTTP responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP responses for JavaScript containing Canvas fingerprinting (canvas.toDataURL), WebGL queries, navigator.userAgent collection, or similar browser/system enumeration patterns. Correlate with ClickFix domain access for higher fidelity.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Download and Execution Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'macOS malware lures'—expected attack chain is user clicks phishing link → browser fingerprinting evaluates victim → conditional malware download → execution. No detection for the download/exec stages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious macOS downloads from ClickFix domains (unusual file types, unsigned binaries, .dmg/.pkg archives from web sources). Correlate file creation with process execution of newly downloaded files within minutes of browsing malicious domains.

suggestion.title: User-Initiated Malicious Link Click from Phishing Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix operates via social engineering lures delivered through 'phishing' (inferred from 'malware lures' in article title and ClickFix's known modus operandi). No detection for user clicking malicious links.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET/POST requests to ClickFix domains originating from user browsers, especially from email client contexts or after user interaction timestamps. Flag domains not previously seen in organization's baseline.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT API Abuse by Fraud Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using ChatGPT across multiple fraud schemes' — pipeline must detect API key compromise and mass-generation patterns consistent with scam automation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ChatGPT API calls with anomalous patterns: tokens from unregistered IPs, high volume identical prompts, geographic mismatch vs account registration, or API keys linked to phishing/fraud infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Poipet Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: fraud network inherently relies on initial-access phishing. Pipeline missed all T1566/T1598 techniques despite scam-network context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate high-volume phishing URLs and sender addresses with Poipet domain registrations and hosting ASNs; alert on clicks followed by credential submission and downstream ChatGPT account adds.

suggestion.title: Detect Compromised ChatGPT and Email Accounts in Fraud Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Article: multiple schemes require account access. Pipeline extracted zero credential-access or account-compromise techniques despite scam operation context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on login anomalies (impossible travel, new device, unusual time-of-day) for accounts later enriched in fraud campaigns; detect shared session tokens; correlate mass login failures with Poipet infrastructure time windows.

suggestion.title: Poipet Infrastructure and Hosting Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: OpenAI 'disrupts' network implies infrastructure seizure. Pipeline extracted zero C2/hosting IOCs despite disruption event narrative
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index domains, registrars, hosting providers, and ASNs associated with Poipet from OpenAI/law-enforcement disclosure; alert on DNS resolutions and connection attempts; correlate hosting changes vs disruption timeline.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing and Scam Content Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article: ChatGPT weaponization for fraud. Pipeline missed detection of AI-model-generated text artifacts and linguistic signatures in captured phishing/scam messages
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint ChatGPT-generated phishing emails (prompt-injection markers, grammar/style consistency, known generation patterns); correlate appearance in captured campaign materials with Poipet threat-intel timeline and confirmed fraud infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Poipet-Related Victim Account Takeover Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'multiple fraud schemes' implying downstream credential use. Pipeline found no post-compromise persistence or impact-phase detections
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track newly compromised user accounts for unusual forwarding rules, mass email sends, or account-recovery attempts; correlate with ChatGPT API usage spikes and phishing-campaign reply-rates.

suggestion.title: Android Device Masquerading as Phone
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states boxes 'pose as phones'—direct reference to T1036.004 Masquerading. Core defense-evasion behavior requiring detection of spoofed device identity in authentication telemetry and network profiles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication attempts where device hardware fingerprint (CPU, model, OS build) indicates TV box or Android but device claims to be phone model. Correlate User-Agent spoofing (phone UA from TV OS) with authentication source IP/device ID mismatch.

suggestion.title: Proxy Service Operation from Consumer IoT
suggestion.rationale: Core impact: boxes 'turn owners' broadband into proxies.' Detect HTTP/SOCKS proxy traffic and relay behavior from TV box endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CONNECT-method HTTP traffic, SOCKS handshakes, or tunneling protocols originating from TV box or Android devices to multiple egress destinations. Correlate with sustained bandwidth anomalies (>10x baseline) and outbound connection to non-whitelisted foreign IPs.

suggestion.title: Botnet Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Organized proxy monetization requires C2 infrastructure and ongoing command relay. Detect callback patterns and secondary payload staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TV box / Android devices for DNS queries to dynamic-DNS providers, bulletproof-hosted domains, or known malware C2 ranges. Alert on non-standard ports (8080, 3128, 8888, 9999) used for C2 heartbeat or proxy advertisement.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Sideloaded APK
suggestion.rationale: Cheap Android TV boxes referenced as pre-infected vector. Detect suspicious APK installation, especially on devices lacking secure boot or with relaxed sideload policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or certificate-pinned APK installations from budget device manufacturers. Flag APKs with INTERNET + CAMERA + FINE_LOCATION + DISABLE_KEYGUARD permissions shipped pre-installed or installed at boot time.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Behavior from Budget Device Maker
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'cheap' boxes by manufacturer—likely identifiable by device model or OEM signature. Establish baseline detection for known-compromised hardware families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create baseline network profiles for known Android TV box manufacturers mentioned in article (extract from full text). Flag any device with matching model/OEM that exhibits proxy relay, C2 callback, or scanning behavior diverging from legitimate streaming use case.

suggestion.title: Device Enrollment Spoofing in MDM/AAD
suggestion.rationale: If TV boxes masquerade as phones to evade geofencing or device-policy controls, detect anomalous enrollment patterns and device-claim validation failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MDM enrollment from devices with TV box identifiers claiming phone OS/model. Flag compliance check failures where device reports mismatched hardware vs. claimed device type. Detect rapid churn in device enrollment/de-enrollment from same physical location.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 TeamCity Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' Pipeline generated zero use cases to hunt exploitation attempts on this protocol.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/HTTPS connections to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (typically port 8111) from external networks or with suspicious deserialization payloads. Look for POST requests to `/agent/` paths with unusual binary/Java serialized object markers (AC ED 05 00 hex, java.io.Serializable signatures) in request bodies.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Unauthenticated Admin Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated remote code execution'—the absence of auth requirement is the core risk vector, distinct from mere exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity web interface (`:8111`) for unauthenticated access to sensitive endpoints (admin console, agent configuration, build queues). Baseline expected auth patterns and flag requests that bypass login or reach admin paths without session tokens.

suggestion.title: TeamCity RCE Code Execution Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote code execution via deserialization'—the post-exploitation execution phase needs its own detection to catch successful attacks, not just exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity Java process (catalina, java.exe, or wrapper process). RCE via deserialization typically spawns shells, reverse-shells, or data exfiltration utilities. Flag anomalous process lineage: TeamCity → cmd.exe/bash/powershell/curl/nc.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Instance Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means active exploitation—initial step is identifying all exposed instances. Article does not mention IOCs for discovery but this is foundational for remediation triage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all TeamCity instances on network/cloud by port scan (:8111, :8112 agent port), SSL certificate search (TeamCity CN patterns), or cloud metadata API queries (AWS Security Groups, Azure NSGs allowing 8111 inbound from 0.0.0.0/0).

suggestion.title: Deserialization Attack Pattern in Java Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the root cause. Generic Java deserialization detection (ysoserial gadgets, unsafe ObjectInputStream usage) applies across TeamCity patches and variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Java serialized object signatures in HTTP request bodies: hex patterns AC ED 05 00 (Java serialization magic bytes), base64-encoded equivalents, or known ysoserial payload markers. High-fidelity if originating from external/untrusted networks to TeamCity.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Exposed to Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' and references 'public-facing application' — detection must establish baseline exposure before exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to TeamCity default ports (8111, 9090, 8112) from external/untrusted network ranges. Correlate with asset inventory to identify publicly routable instances. Alert on any connection attempt to these ports crossing DMZ or internet boundary.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Malformed Request
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'via the agent polling protocol' as the exclusive attack vector — this protocol conversation is the exploitation pathway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag agent polling protocol requests containing serialized Java payloads, overly long request bodies, or protocol structure violations. Cross-reference with known ysoserial gadget chain patterns if TLS inspection available.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Payload in TeamCity Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is specifically 'deserialization of untrusted data' — exploit delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect serialized Java object markers (0xaced0005) in HTTP POST bodies to TeamCity agent endpoints. Alert on requests to /agent/ paths carrying suspicious gadget chain libraries (commons-collections, spring-core, etc.).

suggestion.title: Command Execution from TeamCity Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article guarantees 'remote code execution' outcome; post-exploit child process spawning is inevitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity JVM process (java.exe or /usr/lib/jvm processes), especially shells (cmd.exe, bash, /bin/sh) or utilities (powershell.exe, curl, wget). Flag first-time process spawning from TeamCity service context.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Plugin Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker maintains access via plugin installation — common persistence in Java application servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity plugins directory and buildAgent/plugins for unauthorized additions or modifications. Alert on new .zip or .jar files appearing without deployment workflow approval. Track config.xml mutations for new plugin registration entries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08' and lists in CISA KEV, meaning compliance is regulatory requirement and patch lag correlates with breach risk.

Alert if patch deadline passes without remediation or rollback plan. Correlate scanner inventory with deployment records to identify drift.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Service Discovery & Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability affects exposed TeamCity instances; no asset-hunting UC was generated. 'Unauthenticated remote code execution' implies public-facing exposure requiring baseline inventory before hunting exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for TeamCity service fingerprints (port 8080/8443 by default, HTTP headers 'TeamCity', agent-api endpoints). Correlate against patch inventory to flag CVE-2026-63077 vulnerable versions prior to agent-polling exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent-polling endpoints (typically /update or /connect) for requests with serialized Java objects, encoded payloads, or anomalous Content-Type headers. Flag unauthenticated connections attempting object deserialization.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Successful deserialization RCE results in code execution; article confirms 'remote code execution' but pipeline generated no post-compromise detection. Monitor for process creation or command execution spawned by TeamCity service/process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) spawned by TeamCity process (java.exe or catalina). Cross-reference with TeamCity access logs to correlate timing of agent-polling requests with process creation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Match

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Patterns in Network Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Core mechanism is 'deserialization of untrusted data'; no network-level detection for Java serialization magic bytes or YSOSERIAL-pattern payloads transiting the agent polling protocol.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Java serialization stream headers (0xACED0005) or known RCE gadget chain patterns (CommonsCollections, YSOSERIAL) in HTTP POST bodies to TeamCity agent endpoints. Baseline against legitimate agent traffic to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Exposed Instance Detection

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent polling endpoint traffic for: (a) connections from non-agent IP ranges, (b) malformed polling requests (missing expected headers or auth tokens), (c) large payload sizes suggesting serialized object injection, (d) connection duration anomalies (rapid connect/disconnect), (e) failed HTTP responses (500) followed by outbound connections from TeamCity process.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation TeamCity Process Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE consequence but pipeline generated no post-execution detection. Unauthenticated RCE implies attacker gains code execution in TeamCity process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by TeamCity (java.exe / jre) processes with unusual characteristics: command-line containing powershell/cmd/bash, network connections (curl/wget), file access to sensitive directories, or scheduled task creation. Correlate timing with HTTP requests to agent polling endpoint received within 10 seconds prior.

suggestion.title: L1 Guest Process Invoking Hypervisor Exit Handlers via Zapscape
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Privileged L1 Guest Code Escape to Linux Hosts'—guest process in L1 VM exploiting flaw to reach host kernel. Pipeline generated zero UCs for guest-to-host escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for L1 guest processes executing unusual ioctl() calls against /dev/kvm or hypervisor device nodes, or triggering unexpected EPT violations / MMIO faults from user-mode contexts. Flag guest processes attempting to read/write MSRs or CPU state outside normal VM boundary.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Guest VM Process Memory Access Beyond VM Boundary
suggestion.rationale: Escape exploits abuse host memory mapping or address translation; guest code crossing into host kernel space indicates active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect memory access patterns from guest processes that resolve to host kernel addresses or marked as hypervisor-only. Correlate with privilege level changes, unexpected page-fault handlers triggered, or guest attempting to directly manipulate EPT tables.

suggestion.title: Host Kernel Module Injection from Guest VM Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful escape enables guest to persist in host via kernel module; article states flaw leads to 'escape to Linux Hosts' implying post-escape impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when insmod, modprobe, or kmod operations originate from processes with VM guest identity or anomalous privilege elevation. Monitor /sys/module and kernel symbol table modifications; correlate timing with prior L1 guest hypervisor calls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious IOCTL Sequence Against /dev/kvm from Unprivileged Guest Process
suggestion.rationale: Zapscape likely exploits specific ioctl interaction pattern; unprivileged guest process invoking these calls is anomalous and indicative of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Zapscape flaw sequence is documented (e.g., specific ioctl codes, argument patterns), create rate-based or signature detection for those calls from guest context. Monitor for clusters of failed ioctl attempts followed by successful ones, or ioctl calls with malformed pointers targeting kernel memory.

suggestion.title: L1 Guest CPU Exception Handling Abuse Leading to Hypervisor Escape
suggestion.rationale: Hypervisor flaws often exploit exception handling or CPU mode transitions; article emphasizes guest-level privilege escaping to host, implying CPU-level control-flow manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual VM-exit reasons (e.g., undefined exit codes, double-faults, or exception combinations rarely seen in legitimate workloads). Detect L1 guest processes registering exception handlers in host address space or guest exception-handling code that routes to kernel-mode functions.

suggestion.title: Interrupt Injection Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'New Interrupt Injection Attack' — the attack vector involves manipulating CPU interrupt handling to cross privilege boundaries and bypass isolation mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal interrupt state transitions, rapid context switches between privilege levels, or direct manipulation of interrupt descriptor tables (IDT) from unprivileged code contexts.

suggestion.title: Spectre v2 Mitigation Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass Spectre v2 defenses on Intel and AMD CPUs' — explicitly targets BTB/branch prediction mitigations (IBRS, STIBP).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for disabled/bypassed Spectre v2 mitigations, anomalous branch prediction behavior, or mismatches between advertised and actual CPU mitigation status during suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: CPU Cache Timing Side-Channel Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: interrupt injection enables side-channel attacks through CPU cache state observation; timing-based information leakage is the implied impact of the bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal CPU cache coherency patterns, unusual L1/L3 cache hit/miss ratios per process, or high-frequency performance counter sampling indicative of cache-timing attacks.

suggestion.title: Interrupt Descriptor Table (IDT) Manipulation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'interrupt injection attack' directly implies redirection of CPU exception/interrupt handlers via IDT modification to achieve the bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LIDT (Load IDT Register) execution from user mode, write operations to kernel-mode IDT regions, or registration of custom CPU exception handlers outside approved kernel components.

suggestion.title: Cross-Process Memory Access via Interrupt Timing Covert Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article: the attack 'can bypass Spectre v2 defenses' implies capability to extract data from protected memory (kernel or other processes) using interrupt-based timing measurements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained patterns of fine-grained timing measurements on CPU operations, high-frequency RDPMC/performance counter reads, or processes exhibiting data-dependent cache access latencies across privilege boundaries.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process spawning characteristic of Odysseus family (unsigned child processes from system binaries, script interpreters executing obfuscated payloads, reverse shell indicators). Correlate with C2 beaconing patterns and file hash signatures from threat feeds.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected restarts of TeamCity service (java.exe for TeamCity). Alert on modifications to TeamCity config files (buildAgent.properties, server.xml) not preceded by approved change tickets. Track installation of new agents or plugins without corresponding administrative requests.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation (TeamCity Agents / Plugins)
suggestion.rationale: RCE via deserialization is point-of-entry; attackers typically install persistence via plugins or rogue agents. Article mentions 'agent polling protocol'—this is the persistence vector. No UC for post-compromise agent/plugin activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity plugins directory for unexpected .jar files added outside maintenance windows. Alert on new agent registration events from unusual IP blocks or with suspicious system information in agent details. Track TeamCity configuration changes that enable new agent auto-authorization or modify agent connection security settings.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Service Exposure – CVE-2026-63077
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' Primary detection vector is exposed TeamCity instances reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound connections to TeamCity service ports (default 8111) from external/untrusted networks. Correlate with successful TCP handshake completion and agent polling protocol negotiation patterns.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection – TeamCity Agent Polling
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'deserialization of untrusted data' in agent polling handler. Application-level detection required to identify malicious serialized object payloads before RCE execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoints for serialized Java object payloads with suspicious entropy, gadget chain markers, or blacklisted deserialization classes. Baseline normal polling traffic first.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from TeamCity Agent Context
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation: 'unauthenticated remote code execution' manifests as command execution with TeamCity agent/service as parent process or privilege context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation where parent is TeamCity agent (java.exe with TeamCity arguments). Alert on unexpected child processes, especially cmd/powershell/bash, or outbound network connections from TeamCity contexts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised TeamCity Host
suggestion.rationale: CRIT severity and KEV status indicate active exploitation chains. Compromised TeamCity (CI/CD system) provides privileged network access for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for SMB, RDP, SSH, or Kerberos authentication attempts originating from TeamCity hosts to other corporate assets. Monitor for port scanning or service enumeration initiated from TeamCity service accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Build Configuration Changes – TeamCity Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence: attackers modify build pipelines, agent definitions, or scheduled tasks to maintain access and distribute malicious artifacts across the supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation/modification of build step definitions, agent configurations, or scheduled tasks outside normal change-control procedures. Flag builds triggered at odd hours, pulling from unknown artifact repositories, or containing command-injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from TeamCity Configuration
suggestion.rationale: TeamCity stores API tokens, database credentials, and integration secrets; compromised instances yield high-value credential cache. Article silence on exfiltration does not rule it out given CRIT+KEV status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to TeamCity config.xml, secrets/ directories, and encrypted credential stores from anomalous processes. Flag exports or bulk reads of credential material, or access to TeamCity database credential tables.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Status & Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV and federal due date 2026-08-08; canonical asset-exposure hunt is referenced but not instantiated. No vulnerability scanner rules generated despite this being the detection baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all TeamCity instances in estate; cross-reference against CVE-2026-63077 patch status and internet exposure (port 8111 or agent discovery ports). Prioritize instances with versions prior to patched release. Given CISA KEV active-exploitation status, assume compromise risk is non-zero even if patched—correlate with inbound network traffic to agent polling endpoints.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Inbound Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'agent polling protocol' as attack vector; no network detection rule captures exploitation attempts on this protocol. This is the earliest indicator of active attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (typically auto-discovery or TCP 9090) from external sources followed by malformed or suspicious payloads. Flag deserialization-related error responses (5xx, serialization exceptions) or timeout behavior indicative of exploitation attempts against the untrusted-data vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from TeamCity Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms RCE outcome ('unauthenticated remote code execution'); no behavioral detection rule captures process spawning from TeamCity Java process post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from TeamCity server Java process (java.exe or TeamCity agent services) with anomalous command lines (shell invocation, LOLBin execution, stageless payloads). Baseline normal TeamCity process behavior first; alerting should focus on deviations correlating with network exploitation timeline or unauthenticated inbound activity.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Exception Pattern in TeamCity Logs
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'deserialization of untrusted data'—application logs will expose serialization errors during exploitation. No log-based detection rule was generated for this telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt TeamCity application and agent logs for Java deserialization exceptions (ObjectInputStream errors, ClassNotFoundException, SerialVersionUID mismatches, InvalidClassException) clustered within seconds of inbound agent polling protocol traffic from external IPs. Failed deserialization attempts are often logged before successful exploitation; this provides early warning window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated External Connection to TeamCity Agent Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation is unauthenticated; article states 'via the agent polling protocol' without authentication requirement. No rule detects absence of auth alongside agent protocol activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound connections to agent polling endpoints from external sources with authentication logs—flag cases where agent protocol traffic is observed but no successful authentication event precedes it. Unauthenticated exploitation means RCE happens before login, so absence of auth success + presence of subsequent process execution or error spikes = high-confidence compromise signal.

suggestion.title: Outbound Lateral Movement or Data Exfiltration Post-RCE

Establish TeamCity baseline network egress; alert on anomalous destinations, protocols, or timing patterns that suggest command-and-control or data exfiltration. Correlate with process-creation anomalies for confidence scoring.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference CISA KEV feed against internal vulnerability scanner output, filtered to TeamCity product. Track patch application timeline and flag instances still unpatched 48h before federal due-date (2026-08-06) for escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Agent Polling Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—need detection for requests to agent endpoints without auth headers or from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (e.g. /admin/remote-run, /mnt, agent API paths) from external IPs or lacking Authorization headers. Flag successful 200/302 responses to unauthenticated agent endpoints, particularly from non-corporate ASNs.

suggestion.title: Serialized Java Objects in TeamCity HTTP Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'deserialization of untrusted data'—ysoserial gadget chains and serialized Java objects (magic bytes: ac ed 00 05) indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST bodies to TeamCity for Java serialized object magic bytes or Base64-encoded gadget chains (CommonsCollections, Spring Framework exploits). Alert on ysoserial payloads or known deserialization gadgets in agent polling protocol traffic.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing TeamCity Inventory and Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes public-facing application vulnerability actively exploited—organizations must discover and patch exposed TeamCity instances before 2026-08-08 federal due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and network discovery for TeamCity servers (port 8080, HTTP banner matching, certificate CN). Cross-reference with CMDB to identify instances accepting inbound traffic from public IPs. Correlate with patch status to surface unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Process Spawning from TeamCity Services
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote code execution'—successful exploitation triggers child processes (cmd.exe, powershell, reverse shells) from TeamCity runtime, detectable post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal TeamCity process trees. Alert on java.exe (TeamCity) or teamcity-agent spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wget, curl, bash, or known reverse-shell utilities with minimal historical precedent.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Verification (CISA KEV)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandate: 'Federal patch due 2026-08-08', actively exploited. Patch status is primary control; scanner-based compliance is baseline defensive action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run authenticated vulnerability scan across all TeamCity assets; flag instances reporting CVE-2026-63077 present. Correlate deployed version against JetBrains advisory remediation versions and generate escalation if unpatched past 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article states TeamCity 'contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability' — vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Nessus) will flag this CVE on exposed instances. Direct asset-exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scan results or CMDB patch-compliance queries reporting CVE-2026-63077 on any TeamCity instance. Cross-reference with asset inventory to prioritize exposed services. Federal patch due is 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'agent polling protocol' as the exploitation vector and emphasizes 'unauthenticated' access. Network baseline should flag anomalous inbound connections to the TeamCity agent port (typically 9090).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound traffic to TeamCity on the agent polling port from external or untrusted subnets without corresponding authentication handshake logs. Baseline expected agent IPs and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Process Execution After RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in 'unauthenticated remote code execution' — post-compromise activity should surface as TeamCity service spawning unexpected child processes or commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TeamCity service account executing shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) or suspicious child processes. Establish baseline of legitimate TeamCity child processes and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection in Agent Polling Traffic
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is specifically 'deserialization of untrusted data' — IDS/IPS and DLP should have signatures for serialized Java object payloads in agent polling protocol frames.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: IDS/IPS rule set should include signatures for Java serialization gadget chains (ysoserial payloads, Commons Collections, etc.) traversing the TeamCity agent polling protocol. Alert on any match before application-layer filtering.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance — TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 by Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV articles always include a federal patch deadline ('Federal patch due: 2026-08-08'). Compliance queries and ticketing must reflect this hard date for auditor and regulatory inquiries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch-management or CMDB for TeamCity instances not updated to patched version by 2026-08-08. Generate compliance report and escalate to asset owners. Document any exceptions for audit trail.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised TeamCity Agent
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE via agent polling protocol gives attacker foothold on a build-infrastructure host — likely avenue for lateral movement to other CI/CD systems, repositories, or production infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, monitor for unusual outbound connections or lateral SMB/SSH activity from TeamCity server to other infrastructure. Correlate with RCE indicators (unusual TeamCity process spawning) to catch early lateral-movement chains.

suggestion.title: TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states this is in CISA KEV (actively exploited), with CVE-2026-63077 as the identifier and federal patch due 2026-08-08. Pipeline must generate vulnerability hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan inventory for JetBrains TeamCity instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-63077. Priority: all internet-facing or exposed instances. Cross-reference asset inventory against CISA KEV database and vendor patch advisories. Alert on any instance not patched by federal due date 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' Pipeline must generate detection for unauthorized agent communication attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity application logs and network traffic for agent polling protocol requests from unexpected sources. Flag any unauthenticated agent polling attempts, especially those followed by process creation or command execution. Correlate with TeamCity access logs for non-admin users initiating polling requests.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Attack Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the root mechanism. This is a common gadget-chain exploitation vector that should trigger detection when observed in TeamCity request payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity application logs for serialization/deserialization errors or exceptions. Look for HTTP POST requests to agent polling endpoints with binary/base64-encoded payloads. Alert on process spawning (cmd.exe, bash, powershell) with parent process TeamCity or Java runtime immediately after suspicious HTTP activity.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Patch Compliance Verification (Federal Deadline)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08.' CISA KEV entries trigger compliance requirements for federal agencies; enterprises must track this as audit-material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management systems and vulnerability scanners for TeamCity patch status. Verify all instances have been upgraded to patched version before 2026-08-08. Generate exception report for any unpatched instances with justification and timeline. Cross-reference against CISA KEV federal due-date for audit readiness.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed TeamCity Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article context (CISA KEV, active exploitation, public-facing application attack) implies the risk is from internet-facing TeamCity deployments. Asset exposure hunt must be prioritized.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for TeamCity instances accessible from the internet via port 8111 (default) or other common ports. Cross-reference public DNS records, certificate transparency logs, and Shodan/Censys for TeamCity hostnames/IPs. Flag any internet-facing instances for immediate patch/segmentation review.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Exposed Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly frames this as 'exploit public-facing application' — need to enumerate internet-accessible TeamCity instances before attacker finds them. Prerequisite hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for TeamCity default ports (8111, 80, 443) accessible from internet. Cross-reference Shodan/Censys queries with asset inventory. Flag any exposed instances not explicitly documented as intentionally public.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Agent Polling Protocol Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation 'via the agent polling protocol' — need network-level detection for malformed or oversized polling requests that could deliver deserialization payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent-polling endpoints for unusual request sizes, non-standard headers, repeated failures (deserialization errors), or requests from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with high-entropy payload indicators.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via TeamCity Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution' — post-exploitation phase requires detection of command execution spawned from TeamCity JVM process, particularly unexpected child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by TeamCity java.exe/java process: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, wget, curl, nc. Especially suspicious if spawned without prior build job context or from unexpected build stages.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Outbound C2 Connections Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: After RCE succeeds, attackers typically establish C2 or exfiltration channels — need to detect unexpected network connections initiated by TeamCity process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound network connections from TeamCity process to non-whitelisted destinations, especially on unusual ports (4444, 5555, 8080, 443 with anomalous TLS handshake patterns). Monitor DNS queries from TeamCity context for C2 domain patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires active scanning — basic hygiene is to match vulnerability scanner output for this specific CVE against managed asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CVE-2026-63077 matches from vulnerability scanners with asset management database. Escalate any matches immediately; cross-reference patch management system to confirm remediation status and patch application date.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Error Spikes in TeamCity Logs
suggestion.rationale: Failed exploitation attempts will generate deserialization exceptions in application logs — error pattern can be early warning of active scanning/probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity logs for sudden increase in java.io.NotSerializableException, InvalidClassException, or ClassNotFoundException errors, especially clustered in time or originating from single source IP. Baseline normal error rates first.

suggestion.title: TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 Exploitation Attempts Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—this is the primary attack surface. Pipeline generated zero use cases for the known-exploited vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity /RPC2 and agent polling endpoints for serialized object payloads, POST requests from unusual sources, and error responses consistent with exploit attempts. Track HTTP 500 errors and exception logs coinciding with malformed requests.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Registration Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation via agent polling allows attacker-controlled agent registration. Article describes 'agent polling protocol'—agents are the execution primitive after compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new agent registrations with mismatched hostnames/IPs, agents from unexpected networks, and sudden spikes in agent build queue activity post-vulnerability window (2026-08-08 patch date).

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Instance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status implies widespread internet-facing TeamCity installations being scanned. Article describes 'public-facing application'—asset inventory is the prerequisite hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all public-facing TeamCity instances (default ports 8111/8112) and cross-reference against patched versions. Flag instances still running builds post-patch-due-date (2026-08-08) without confirmed remediation.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'deserialization of untrusted data'. Pipeline missed the serialization-specific attack surface—standard HTTP monitoring won't catch crafted binary payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling traffic for Java serialization magic bytes (ACED0005), unusual ysoserial gadget chain indicators, and ClassNotFound exceptions in agent logs during exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Creation from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE will spawn attacker commands. Article describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution'—post-exploitation command execution is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity JVM (java.exe), especially shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or lateral-movement tools. Baseline TeamCity process behavior and flag deviations post-2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Scan Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal remediation by 2026-08-08. Pipeline should have produced a compliance-hunting template—zero UCs means scanning strategy is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-validate vuln scanner detections for CVE-2026-63077 against actual patched versions in asset database. Identify scanner false-negatives (claimed patched but exploit still functional) and validate all TeamCity instances ≤2026-08-08 show remediation evidence in patch logs.

suggestion.title: Redis Public-Facing Service Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links TeamPCP to 'Redis Attacks' — initial access vector should have been reconstructed. Expects detection for CVE exploitation or unauthenticated Redis protocol abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to TCP 6379 (Redis default) from untrusted IP ranges; flag successful commands without prior authentication handshake; correlate with known Redis RCE payloads (e.g., MODULE LOAD, SCRIPT commands).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis Authentication Credentials Cached
suggestion.rationale: Redis supply chain compromise often involves credential harvesting or hardcoded auth tokens. Article mentions 'Supply Chain Campaign'—credentials are the pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for plaintext Redis credentials in process arguments (–requirepass, CONFIG SET password), environment variables, or config files in suspicious locations; correlate with package installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Modification or Metadata Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Later Supply Chain Campaign'—pipeline should detect repository poisoning, package signing violations, or deployment of modified package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package version downgrades, unsigned or revoked-certificate packages, packages delivered outside normal CI/CD, or hash mismatches against official repositories.

suggestion.title: TeamPCP C2 Infrastructure Communication
suggestion.rationale: Redis compromise is an entry point; article dating back to 2020 suggests persistent C2 infrastructure associated with TeamPCP. Should detect known TeamPCP C2 domains, IPs, or TLS certificates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network egress from Redis-compromised hosts against known TeamPCP OSINT (domain registrations, ASN patterns, certificate CN/SANs); flag anomalous outbound protocols or suspicious TLS renegotiations.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Redis Command Sequence (Lateral Movement)
suggestion.rationale: After Redis compromise, attacker executes reconnaissance and lateral movement. Article timeline (2020+) suggests multi-stage attack; pipeline should detect suspicious Redis KEYS, SCAN, or data exfiltration commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis command logs for KEYS *, SCAN 0, AUTH attempts with common/weak credentials, or unexpected DUMP/MIGRATE commands; correlate timing with exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: Malware Dropper via Compromised Redis Data Structure
suggestion.rationale: Redis module loading (MODULE LOAD) or serialized-object deserialization can execute arbitrary code. Supply chain context implies packaged payloads; should detect suspicious binary or script storage in Redis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Redis MODULE LOAD followed by child process spawning; detect unusual script or binary serialization in Redis key-value pairs; correlate with supply chain artifact timestamps.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes self-propagating npm worm; worms typically persist via lifecycle scripts. Article body should detail install/postinstall hook execution. No UC generated despite this being core malware behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/uninstall operations preceded by unexpected child processes spawning shell interpreters. Alert on env vars passed to postinstall scripts, especially those accessing secrets or making outbound network calls.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Environment Variable Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states worm 'extracting GitHub Actions runner secrets.' No UC maps credential access from CI/CD secrets. This is the attack's high-value vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes reading GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, or other CI/CD secrets from environment within npm module code paths. Flag data exfiltration via DNS TXT records, base64 in HTTP headers, or blockchain contract calls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ethereum Smart Contract Interaction from npm Module
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Ethereum smart contracts for C2 routing.' Pipeline generated zero C2 detection. This is anomalous network behavior—npm modules should not initiate blockchain transactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes making HTTP/HTTPS connections to blockchain RPC endpoints (infura.io, alchemy.com, etherscan.io) or resolving Ethereum contract addresses. Flag payload encoding within contract call parameters (0x... patterns in data field).

suggestion.title: npm Module Self-Propagation via Dependency Graph Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Self-Propagating npm Worm.' Worms must replicate. No UC detects malicious dependency injection or package.json modification during install. This is the propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json modifications (additions to dependencies, devDependencies, or version downgrades) and npm registry auth token usage from non-privileged accounts. Flag npm publish operations from compromised package contexts.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from node_modules with Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Worm must execute malicious code post-install. Article provides no specific detection hypothesis, but npm malware signature is child process spawning from node_modules tree with outbound network calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation from node_modules/.bin or node_modules/<package>/lib paths with subsequent DNS/TLS connections to attacker infrastructure. Baseline legitimate package binary usage; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Disclosure in Logs or Temporary Files
suggestion.rationale: If secrets are exfiltrated, they may be staged in logs, environment dumps, or temp files. No UC maps this ex-filtration pattern specific to CI/CD secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm install output logs and temp directories for leaked GitHub tokens (ghp_* patterns), AWS keys, or Ethereum private keys. Cross-reference file modification times against malicious package install timestamps.

suggestion.title: Vishing with Passkey/MFA Update Pretexting
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'UNC6671 operators typically contact employees on their personal mobile phones while spoofing corporate help-desks and claiming that workers need to enroll in passkeys or update their multi-factor authentication settings.' No detection use case for inbound social engineering calls followed by credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound calls claiming to originate from corporate helpdesk (via caller ID spoofing detection) with failed or successful SSO authentication attempts occurring within 30 minutes from unusual geographies. Alert on patterns of employees reporting helpdesk verification calls followed by credential-reset or multi-factor-authentication enrollment events.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Kit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Victims are then directed to domains impersonating the targeted employee's company that host adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits designed to steal credentials and session cookies in real time.' No UC for detecting credential harvesting via lookalike domain hosting or session cookie interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains similar to corporate identity (typosquats, subdomain spoofs). Flag SSL certificates issued within days for domains impersonating known corporate infrastructure. Correlate failed authentication attempts to legitimate SSO endpoints with proxy traffic to lookalike domains in the same time window.

suggestion.title: Bulk Automated Cloud Data Exfiltration via Compromised SSO
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'After stealing Microsoft 365 or Okta single-sign-on accounts, the attackers log into the SSO dashboard, which gives access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account... hackers then use automated tools to steal data from all cloud services they gain access to.' No UC for detecting automated enumeration and bulk exfiltration across linked cloud platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSO sign-ins from new geographies immediately following vishing campaigns. Flag rapid, sequential API calls from a single compromised account accessing multiple cloud services (>10 apps in 15 minutes). Detect automated downloads of large numbers of files or calendar/mail objects from OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, or third-party cloud apps within minutes of SSO compromise.

suggestion.title: Security Notification and Password-Reset Email Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'delete security notifications and password-reset emails from compromised inboxes.' No UC for detecting adversary suppression of security alerts or password-reset communications post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk email deletions (>50 emails in 5 minutes) or rapid moves to deleted items, especially emails from security teams, helpdesk, or containing password-reset or MFA-verification keywords. Alert when security notifications or password-reset emails are deleted before being read or within seconds of arrival by a user who shows no prior email deletion patterns.

suggestion.title: Multi-Platform Lateral Movement via Stolen SSO Session Cookies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'After stealing Microsoft 365 or Okta single-sign-on accounts, the attackers log into the SSO dashboard, which gives access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account.' No UC for detecting lateral movement across multiple cloud platforms using session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication to SSO dashboard consoles from new/unusual IP geographies within hours of initial credential compromise. Flag accounts accessing >8 distinct cloud applications (Microsoft 365, Salesforce, Slack, Workday, etc.) in a single session. Alert on session tokens used to authenticate to multiple platforms from a single source IP without corresponding user-agent diversity.

suggestion.title: Automated Cloud Resource Enumeration Post-SSO Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should detect the discovery phase implied by: 'use automated tools to steal data from all cloud services they gain access to,' indicating system enumeration of available cloud resources and permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid enumeration of cloud application catalogs, Okta app lists, or Azure app registrations (>20 API calls in 2 minutes). Detect queries for permissions, roles, and group memberships via Graph API or Okta APIs immediately post-compromise. Flag when a single account queries cloud resource tags or metadata to discover what data is available before exfiltration.

suggestion.title: KVM Guest-to-Host Privilege Escalation via Hypercall
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'privileged L1 guest code escape to Linux hosts' — escape from guest to host kernel requires abnormal hypercall sequences or KVM instruction emulation exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequences of unusual hypercalls from guest VMs, particularly those attempting to access host kernel address space, modify VMCS structures, or trigger unhandled page faults at host privilege level. Alert on nested VM contexts (L1→L2) attempting cross-level escapes.

suggestion.title: KVM Memory-Mapped I/O Escape Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: KVM escapes commonly exploit MMIO mishandling between guest and host; 'Zapscape' likely leverages improper MMIO boundary checking to read/write host kernel memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or sequential MMIO operations from guest context targeting host-reserved address ranges, or MMIO operations that correlate with subsequent kernel privilege checks being bypassed.

suggestion.title: Host Kernel Code Execution from Guest Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful escape must result in code execution at ring-0; expect kernel panics, privilege escalation syscalls, or unexpected kernel module loads correlating with guest VM activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate guest VM process activity with host kernel panics, BUG() macro triggers, or oops messages. Flag sequences where guest syscalls are immediately followed by root-level code execution on host or unexpected kernel module operations.

suggestion.title: Nested Virtualization L1/L2 Boundary Crossing
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'L1 guest code' — this is nested virtualization. Attacker escapes L1 context to L2 or to host; L1 implies guest-within-guest scenario not typically monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of nested VM configurations where L1 guests attempt to allocate excessive memory, trigger rapid VMEXIT rates, or perform operations inconsistent with normal nested virtualization workloads.

suggestion.title: KVM Kernel Parameter or Data Structure Corruption
suggestion.rationale: Escapes often involve overwriting guest-accessible kernel structures (e.g., modifying KVM pte flags, vCPU state). Article's severity suggests memory corruption vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to kernel virtual address space from guest userspace, or modifications to page table entries via guest-accessible mechanisms. Flag use of mprotect/mmap on /dev/kvm or /dev/mem with CAP_SYS_ADMIN-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Hugging Face Model Repository Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states model repositories as attack surface: 'model repositories execute arbitrary code.' Pipeline missed initial-access detection for reconnaissance-phase downloads from untrusted Hugging Face accounts or newly-created repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git clone or curl downloads from huggingface.co to local directories; flag repos created within last 30 days or from accounts with zero social signals. Alert on Python processes invoking git/curl with homoglyph-variant model names (e.g., diffuser-s vs diffusers).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via Pickle/Safetensors Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'execute arbitrary code' during model load. Diffusers library deserializes model files (pickle, safetensors, pt) during import—standard vector for code injection. Pipeline produced zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Python processes import diffusers.DiffusionPipeline or transformers followed by unexpected child-process spawning, network egress, or file writes outside expected model-cache directories. Inspect for pickle.load(), torch.load() on untrusted paths.

suggestion.title: Model Weight Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Flaws enable code injection 'in model repositories'—attackers can poison weights. Pipeline ignored persistence/supply-chain technique mapping (T1195.001, T1195.002) entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-check downloaded model artifacts (model.safetensors, pytorch_model.bin, config.json) against SHA256 hashes published by Hugging Face or verified sources. Alert on mismatches. Monitor ~/.cache/huggingface for unexpected file modifications.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Poisoning via Model Install
suggestion.rationale: Loading Hugging Face models triggers pip installs of diffusers and transformers; malicious repos can hijack dependencies. Article implies supply-chain code-execution vector; pipeline provided no dependency-hygiene detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip/poetry/uv installs spawned by Python data-science or inference processes. Flag typo-squatted package names, external registry URLs, or installs of packages not in pinned requirements files. Correlate install timestamps with model downloads.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from Model Inference
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'execute arbitrary code'; this manifests as process creation. Pipeline omitted execution-phase detection entirely, leaving subprocess spawning unmonitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal process trees for Python inference workloads. Alert on deviations: parent=python.exe, child=bash/powershell/cmd/sh spawning with suspicious args (curl, wget, nc, reverse-shell markers). Correlate with model-load timestamps from logs.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from Model Inference Process
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution can lead to C2 or data exfiltration. Article emphasizes execution risk; pipeline produced zero command-and-control or exfiltration detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected DNS queries or TCP/TLS connections from Python processes running inference. Flag non-standard ports, known malware C2 domains, cloud-storage URLs, or pastebin/Telegram endpoints. Baseline legitimate model-download traffic (PyPI, Hugging Face) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerable TeamCity Instance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08'—no asset-exposure hunt generated despite template callout in 'Recommended hunts' section. Must detect unpatched or internet-exposed TeamCity instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for internet-exposed TeamCity instances via port enumeration or certificate transparency. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-63077 presence. Flag any instance not patched by 2026-08-08 deadline.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Deserialization Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly 'via the agent polling protocol' with 'deserialization of untrusted data' as root cause—no protocol-specific or payload-based detection generated. Deserialization attacks leave traces in application error logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling protocol (typically port 9090) for unauthenticated connection attempts from non-agent IP ranges. Alert on Java deserialization exceptions, ClassCastException, or InvalidObjectException in TeamCity logs correlating with agent polling.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Post-Exploitation Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article guarantees 'unauthenticated remote code execution' outcome—no post-compromise execution detection generated. Successful exploitation grants arbitrary code execution on TeamCity server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity JVM process (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl). Flag execution not initiated by TeamCity service account or not from expected build agent subprocesses. Baseline normal TeamCity child processes first.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from TeamCity Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation implies active exploitation in wild—attacker with RCE access will target stored credentials. Article context ('federal agencies required to remediate') suggests sensitive pipeline/code access. No credential-hunting detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthorized file access to TeamCity configuration directories (containing stored VCS/cloud credentials), .ssh keys, or agent properties. Monitor for extraction of stored secrets from TeamCity credential storage or access to build logs containing sensitive data.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised TeamCity Pipeline Access
suggestion.rationale: TeamCity controls build pipelines and deployment credentials across development infrastructure—post-compromise, attacker pivots using captured CI/CD permissions. No lateral movement detection generated despite high-value target profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track TeamCity user logins and VCS credential usage from compromised agent. Flag unusual git clone/push/deploy operations, credential usage from non-expected IP/agent, or activation of dormant/service accounts after initial RCE window.
